**RESULT ALREADY PUBLIC:** InnoCare announced on July 15, 2026 that the registrational Phase III trial of soficitinib (ICP-332) met the primary endpoint in patients with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis. The release said the result was statistically significant and clinically meaningful, but I found no numeric effect sizes or p-values. It does not say which of the two registered primary outcomes was met. Source: [GlobeNewswire press release](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/07/15/3327622/0/en/innocare-announces-phase-iii-study-results-of-tyk2-inhibitor-soficitinib-meet-primary-endpoint-in-patients-with-atomic-dermatitis.html). Reports describe the trial as enrolling 579 patients ([AllSci](https://allsci.com/news/clinical-trials/innocare-advances-soficitinib-toward-china-filing-after-positive-phase-iii-atopic-dermatitis-trial/)), versus 552 estimated in the record.

**Earlier trial (Phase 2, NCT05702268):** Published in JAMA Dermatology (2026). Randomized 75 patients, four weeks. The EASI-75 response rate was 64.0% in each dose group, a difference vs placebo of 56.0% (95% CI 34.4%–77.6%; P<.001). The vIGA-AD 0/1 result at 80 mg was 36.0%, difference 32.0% (95% CI 11.7%–52.3%; P=.005). Source: [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41533373/). The Phase 2 primary outcome was safety, and the key efficacy endpoint was percent change in EASI at week 4 ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41533373/)), so it differs from the Phase 3's 16-week endpoints. The small sample gives wide intervals.

**Other diseases, same drug:** An oral TYK2 inhibitor for vitiligo met its Phase 2 primary endpoint. Psoriasis, prurigo nodularis, and urticaria trials are still running ([InnoCare interim results](https://www.innocarepharma.com/uploads/2026-08-24/20260824_InnoCare-Interim-Results_EN.pdf)). I did not find Phase 2 or 3 data for the drug in psoriasis.

**Same mechanism in AD:** I found no approved TYK2 inhibitor for AD ([Patsnap](https://synapse.patsnap.com/article/innocare-begins-phase-iii-trial-of-tyk2-inhibitor-icp-332-for-atopic-dermatitis-in-china)). For the JAK1 class, abrocitinib's JADE MONO-2 reported EASI-75 at week 12 in 61% on 200 mg, 44.5% on 100 mg, and 10.4% of controls ([Medscape](https://www.medscape.com/viewarticle/932889)). Upadacitinib's AD Up trial, given with topical steroids, reported 65/77% EASI-75 on upadacitinib 15/30 mg plus TCS vs 26% on placebo plus TCS at week 16 ([AbbVie](https://news.abbvie.com/2020-07-28-Third-Pivotal-Phase-3-Study-Shows-RINVOQ-TM-upadacitinib-Plus-Topical-Corticosteroids-Improves-Skin-and-Itch-Symptoms-in-Atopic-Dermatitis-Patients)). Placebo arms in these trials have ranged roughly from 10% to 27% EASI-75, so the placebo comparator is not unusually strong.

**Base rate:** I did not find a systematic estimate of how often AD trials meet this endpoint.

**Sponsor statements:** The company said detailed durability, dose-optimization, and longer-term safety data would come at future congresses or journals ([Dermatology Times](https://www.dermatologytimes.com/view/soficitinib-icp-332-meets-primary-endpoint-in-phase-3-trial-for-moderate-to-severe-ad)). It plans an NDA following the completion of the 52-week safety follow-up ([Patsnap](https://synapse.patsnap.com/drug/1026fbb79dda4cfc9ca45a1af4cf9675)). I found nothing on powering, interim analyses, enrollment problems, or design changes for this trial.

**Record caveats:** The record was last updated 2025-09-08 and lists the trial as recruiting. Its primary completion date (2026-11-25) is after the July 2026 topline announcement, so the record is stale. The Phase 2 and Phase 3 results are both from the same sponsor, and Phase 2 authors included company employees ([Medscape](https://www.medscape.com/viewarticle/tyrosine-kinase-2-inhibitor-shows-benefit-atopic-dermatitis-2026a100019m)).

**RESULT ALREADY PUBLIC:** No. ADEPT-4's double-blind result has not been released. Open-label data from sister trials have been, and BMS says the ADEPT trials remain ongoing, and data from the double-blind treatment periods in all ADEPT studies remain blinded. Source: https://investingnews.com/bristol-myers-squibb-presents-first-clinical-data-from-two-phase-3-studies-in-the-adept-program-evaluating-karxt-for-psychosis-associated-with-alzheimer-s-disease/

**Timing and enrollment**
- The record's 2026-11-24 primary completion date conflicts with guidance. In July, CEO Chris Boerner said top-line data readouts for ADEPT-2 and ADEPT-4 would be pushed back to early 2027, from a previous target of later this year, citing the "pace of enrolment". Source: https://firstwordpharma.com/story/8455678
- The delay was attributed to slower enrollment in the Adept-2 and Adept-4 studies and slower relapse event accrual in Adept-1. Source: https://www.fiercepharma.com/pharma/bristol-myers-delays-cobenfy-alzheimers-psychosis-readout-again-amid-another-quarterly-beat
- BMS attributed slow enrollment to efforts to ensure patients meet eligibility criteria (same source, 22-14). The eligibility stringency could limit the population but the record shows no design change.
- Site irregularities hit the sister trial ADEPT-2: a data monitoring committee recommended the trial keep going and enroll more participants so as to hit its original target. Source: https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/bristol-myers-cobenfy-alzheimers-psychosis-adept-2-trial-update-timeline/806917/ I found no report of irregularities at ADEPT-4 sites.

**Earlier KarXT data in this disease (all open-label, uncontrolled)**
- ADEPT-1 lead-in: a mean reduction of 12.0 points from a baseline of 14.4 (n=266) was observed on the NPI-C H+D scale. Source: https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/bristol-myers-squibb-presents-first-clinical-data-from-two-phase-3-studies-in-the-adept-program-evaluating-karxt-for-psychosis-associated-with-alzheimers-disease
- ADEPT-3 (52 weeks): a mean reduction of 5.1 points from an open-label baseline of 8.9 (n=270). Same source. Open-label drops without a placebo arm are hard to interpret.
- ADEPT-1's own primary endpoint is time to relapse event during the 26-week double-blind period, so its randomized data will not directly test ADEPT-4's endpoint.

**Mechanism history in AD**
- Xanomeline, the active component, was tested in a 6-month trial of 343 patients. In the high-dose arm, 52% of patients discontinued treatment because of adverse events. Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9109749/
- Behavioral benefit was a secondary observation: dose-dependent reductions in vocal outbursts, suspiciousness, delusions, agitation, and hallucinations were significant (P ≤ .002), but these came from a treatment-emergent symptom analysis, not a prespecified primary test. Same source.

**Other diseases**
- In schizophrenia, a 400-person schizophrenia study found it not significantly better than a placebo as an add-on treatment to atypical antipsychotics. Source: https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/bristol-myers-cobenfy-alzheimers-psychosis-adept-2-trial-update-timeline/806917/

**Same disease, different mechanism (pimavanserin)**
- The HARMONY trial pooled dementia types. Its overall result was positive, with a >2.8-fold reduction in risk of relapse with pimavanserin (hazard ratio: 0.353; 1-sided p=0.0023). Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7740939/
- The Alzheimer's subgroup was not significant: hazard ratio for psychosis relapse risk with pimavanserin 34mg versus placebo was 0.466 (95% CI: 0.179, 1.214), with 6/57 versus 14/59 relapses. Source: https://alz-journals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/alz.062364

**Base rates and comparator**
- I found no published placebo-response rate or historical success rate for primary endpoints in AD psychosis trials. The forecaster should not assume the comparator is weak or strong based on this search.

**Analyst views**
- After the CTAD open-label data, one analyst said investors were encouraged by the early efficacy signals but said investors are still awaiting more robust randomized results for the therapy. Source: https://www.biospace.com/drug-development/CTAD-2026-bms-cobenfy-eases-alzheimers-psychosis-as-expected-but-safety-events-raise-questions

**RESULT ALREADY PUBLIC:** No. I found no posted result for NCT06693895. A Pharmaconomics calendar entry says results are due November 23, 2026, but that is a third-party date, not a sponsor disclosure ([pharmaconomics.com/e/78](https://pharmaconomics.com/e/78)).

**Earlier trials of this vaccine (VNS, GSK)**
- The phase 2 dose-range trial (NCT05084508) compared three VNS potencies with Varivax in 12–15-month-olds. Its primary immunogenicity endpoint was anti-gE seroresponse. Seroresponse at Day 43 was 93.6–98.7% in the VNS groups and 98.1% in the control, and adverse event rates were similar across groups ([PubMed 41825190](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41825190/)). I did not retrieve sample sizes, p-values, or confidence intervals for the safety comparison.
- Before that trial, the vaccine had never been given to humans, and the sponsor expected a profile similar to Varivax and Varilrix ([protocol amendment](https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/08/NCT05084508/Prot_000.pdf)).
- Background rates for Oka-strain vaccines, from the same protocol: generalized varicella-like rash in about 4–6% of recipients and fever within 42 days in about 15% ([protocol](https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/08/NCT05084508/Prot_000.pdf)). Those figures are useful reference points for the solicited-event outcomes.

**Other diseases and other products with the same mechanism**
- No other indications for VNS turned up.
- Sinovac's Oka-strain vaccine ran a single-dose non-inferiority trial against Varivax in the Philippines, but I did not retrieve its results ([PMC12474105](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12474105/)).
- A differently attenuated Chinese candidate (v7D) was well tolerated in a 224-person placebo-controlled phase 1 ([PubMed 37283962](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37283962/)). This is a different strain modification, so it is only a loose analogue.

**Benchmarks for the comparator**
- Varivax is a strong comparator on efficacy. A 14-year Kaiser cohort reported about 90% effectiveness with no waning ([PubMed 23545380](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/23545380)).
- A network meta-analysis put one-dose Varivax at about 93% efficacy, significantly higher than one-dose GSK's Varilrix ([Synapse summary](https://synapse.patsnap.com/drug/06dc61b5f5d1457db279eeb487e3f938)). This is a secondary source.
- For this trial, Varivax is a reactogenicity benchmark, not an efficacy bar.

**How often this kind of endpoint is met**
- The registry's primary outcomes are descriptive percentages of solicited and unsolicited events. I found no stated success threshold or hypothesis test. Without one, "meeting the endpoint" is undefined. The forecaster should check the statistical analysis plan or the posted protocol.
- I found no data on how often comparable vaccine safety endpoints have been met.

**Sponsor statements**
- I found nothing from GSK or the investigators on powering, interim analyses, enrollment problems, design changes, or delays for this trial.
- GSK's pipeline appendices list the varicella program but give no readout date for this study ([Q3 2026 appendix](https://www.gsk.com/media/k3aasdat/q3-2026-pipeline-assets-and-clinical-trials-report-pdf.pdf)).
- Vaccine pipeline trackers note that company-projected timelines often shift ([Vaccine Data Navigator](https://vaccinedatanavigator.org/vaccine-pipeline.html)). A different GSK varicella trial is listed with a December 2026 readout date ([Vaccine Data Navigator](https://vaccinedatanavigator.org/pipeline/ctgov-investigational-varicella-vaccine-lot-1-glaxosmithkline.html)). That trial is not this one.

**Evidence brief: NCT07057622 (177Lu-DOTATATE vs octreotide LAR, PFS rate at 18 months)**

**Trial-specific status**
- No public result for this trial, and I found no sponsor or investigator statements on powering, interim analyses, enrollment, or delays.
- The record's primary completion date (2026-11-24) conflicts with "recruiting" status and an 18-month PFS landmark. Late enrollees could not reach 18 months by then, so expect the date to slip or be stale. The record was last updated 2025-07-10.
- The title's "Oxytrexine" appears to be a translation error for octreotide; the arm description says octreotide LAR.

**Earlier 177Lu-DOTATATE trials (same drug, same disease, PFS primary)**
- NETTER-1 (midgut NET, progressed on SSA, n=229): median PFS not reached vs 8.4 months, HR 0.21 (0.13–0.33), p<0.001 ([PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7227421/)). PFS at month 20 was 65.2% vs 10.8% ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28076709/)). Both arms included octreotide 30 mg LAR with the 177Lu arm, unlike this trial's monotherapy design.
- NETTER-2 (first-line G2/G3, n=226): median PFS 22.8 vs 8.5 months, stratified HR 0.276 (0.182–0.418), p<0.0001 ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38851203)). ORR was 43% vs 9.3% ([JCO abstract](https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/JCO.2024.42.3_suppl.LBA588)).
- XT-XTR008-3-01 is the closest design analogue: a no-carrier-added 177Lu-DOTATATE monotherapy vs octreotide 60 mg in progressive G1–2 GEP-NETs, with PFS by blinded review. It reported significantly improved PFS and ORR ([Annals of Oncology](https://www.annalsofoncology.org/article/S0923-7534(25)04697-6/fulltext)). I could not retrieve its PFS hazard ratio or medians; check the full paper.

**Other drugs, same mechanism or disease**
- COMPETE (177Lu-edotreotide, an SSTR agonist radioligand, vs everolimus, G1–2, n=309): median PFS 23.9 vs 14.1 months, HR 0.67 (0.48–0.95), p=0.022 ([ITM release](https://www.itm-radiopharma.com/news/press-releases/press-releases-detail/itm-announces-primary-results-from-the-phase-3-compete-trial-published-in-the-lancet-comparing-177lu-edotreotide-itm-11-vs-everolimus-in-advanced-gep-nets-758/)). The PFS benefit was significant only in the second-line subgroup ([Cancer Therapy Advisor](https://www.cancertherapyadvisor.com/reports/177lu-edotreotide-bests-everolimus-in-patients-with-gep-nets/)). This suggests effect sizes shrink outside NETTER-1's population.

**Comparator and base rates**
- Octreotide LAR 60 mg control arms in NETTER-1 and NETTER-2 had median PFS of 8.4–8.5 months, and NETTER-1's control had 10.8% PFS at month 20 (sources above). The comparator is weak on PFS.
- NETTER-1's authors noted that response rates above 5% had not appeared in large RCTs of other systemic therapies in this population ([NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1607427)).
- I did not compile a systematic rate of PFS-endpoint success across GEP-NET trials. The 177Lu-based trials above all met PFS endpoints, but these are selected, mostly sponsor-run examples.

**Forecast notes**
- The key uncertainty is whether monotherapy 177Lu-DOTATATE in a Chinese, mixed-origin population matches the NETTER-1/XT-XTR008 benefit. Both of those trials support a positive direction.
- The record does not show whether an 18-month PFS rate, rather than a median, was powered. With n=184 (estimated), a modest difference could be hard to detect.

**Evidence brief: NCT07122401 (MT1013 vs cinacalcet, SHPT)**

**Result status:** No result is public. A November 2026 company announcement said all 435 enrolled patients finished treatment and follow-up, but the trial remains blinded and primary endpoints are unreported ([Minichart](https://www.minichart.com.sg/2026/11/09/micot-pharmas-mt1013-phase-iii-trial-completes-all-435-patients-results-still-blinded/); [TipRanks](https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/shaanxi-micot-completes-phase-iii-treatment-and-follow-up-for-mt1013)). The company gave no timeline for database lock, unblinding, or analysis ([Minichart](https://www.minichart.com.sg/2026/11/09/micot-pharmas-mt1013-phase-iii-trial-completes-all-435-patients-results-still-blinded/)). The registry's enrollment figure (424, estimated) and single site differ from the company's 435 and "more than 100 sites" ([Everest release](https://www.prnewswire.com/apac/news-releases/everest-medicines-announces-exclusive-license-agreement-with-micot-to-commercialize-mt1013-302679600.html)).

**Earlier MT1013 data (all company-sponsored, abstract-level):**
- Kidney Week 2025 abstract: in MT1013 groups, 83.9% and 93.3% reached >30% iPTH reduction, versus 90.6% with etelcalcetide. For >50%, rates were 74.2% and 76.7% versus 78.1% ([ASN abstract](https://www.asn-online.org/education/kidneyweek/2025/program-abstract.aspx?controlId=4402225)). MT1013 did not beat etelcalcetide on the >50% endpoint.
- A separate JASN abstract (33 patients, uncontrolled) reported >30% reduction in 87.5% at week 24 and 89.7% at week 52, and >50% reduction in 71.9% and 69% ([JASN abstract](https://journals.lww.com/jasn/fulltext/2025/10001/efficacy_and_safety_of_mt1013_in_patients_with.60.aspx)).
- Neither abstract reports p-values, confidence intervals, or a cinacalcet comparison. I found no full publication.

**Same mechanism / cinacalcet as comparator:**
- MT1013 is described as a CaSR agonist plus OGP mimetic ([Ozmosi](https://pryzm.ozmosi.com/product/23119); [Everest](https://www.prnewswire.com/apac/news-releases/everest-medicines-announces-exclusive-license-agreement-with-micot-to-commercialize-mt1013-302679600.html)). One database labels it a PTH1R antagonist, which conflicts with the others ([Synapse](https://synapse.patsnap.com/drug/acb51d70795241ae9ec3d4675fc7ae9c)).
- Cinacalcet's pivotal 10-week phase (n=395, versus placebo) gave ≥30% iPTH reduction in 65% versus 13% ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15689407/)). Pooled 6-month phase 3 data show about 60% reaching ≥30% ([Health Canada monograph](https://pdf.hres.ca/dpd_pm/00062080.PDF)).
- In a pediatric placebo-controlled trial, 55% on cinacalcet reached the ≥30% endpoint versus 19% on placebo ([Pediatric Nephrology](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00467-018-4116-y)).
- A single-arm Korean study found about 17.5% of dialysis patients did not respond to cinacalcet ([PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3575968/)).
- Cinacalcet is an established active comparator. The record does not say whether the trial tests superiority or non-inferiority, and I found no statement of power.

**Sponsor statements:** The company has described MT1013 as showing advantages over current therapy on composite control of iPTH, calcium and phosphate ([Everest](https://www.prnewswire.com/apac/news-releases/everest-medicines-announces-exclusive-license-agreement-with-micot-to-commercialize-mt1013-302679600.html)). That composite comparison was against etelcalcetide in a small Phase II (30.3% versus 12.1%) ([ASN abstract](https://www.asn-online.org/education/kidneyweek/2025/program-abstract.aspx?controlId=4402225)). In February 2026, over 50% of target enrollment was reported as achieved ([Everest](https://www.prnewswire.com/apac/news-releases/everest-medicines-announces-exclusive-license-agreement-with-micot-to-commercialize-mt1013-302679600.html)). I found no statements on interim analyses, powering, or design changes.

**Other indications:** Not searched. Nothing found on MT1013 outside SHPT.

**Gaps:** No full Phase II publication, no p-values from MT1013 studies, no Phase III powering or interim-analysis disclosure, and no database-lock date. The registry's primary completion date (2026-11-26) is not confirmed by the company.

**Evidence brief: NCT07103148 (vYF vs Stamaril/YF-VAX, ages 9 months to 5 years)**

No result for this trial is public. I found no VYF04 results, press release, or sponsor timing statement.

**1. Earlier vYF trials (adults only)**
- The phase 2 adult trial (VYF03, NEJM 2026) used the same primary endpoint, day-29 seroconversion. In the per-protocol population, seroconversion by day 29 occurred in 328 of 329 vYF participants (99.7%) and 155 of 156 YF-VAX participants (99.4%), a difference of 0.3 points (95% CI −1.2 to 3.2). Source: https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2505665
- Noninferiority was defined as a lower CI bound above −5 points. The trial was powered at more than 90% assuming 98% seroconversion (same source).
- Day-11 responses were lower: the trial was not powered to show noninferiority with respect to the early immune response (same source).
- Prior YF immunity lowered day-29 seroconversion, owing to the difficulty in mounting a 4-fold increase when titers are already high (same source).
- The registry describes VYF04 as the first study to be carried out with the investigational vYF in pediatric populations (https://www.sanofi.com/en/clinical-trials/nct07103148). I found no pediatric vYF data.

**2. Other diseases**
- I found no non-yellow-fever data for vYF.

**3. Comparator and pediatric benchmarks**
- In a Brazilian trial of 9–23-month-olds, seroconversion was 84.8% and 85.8% for two 17D substrains (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4667580/). Rates were lower among those aged 12 months or older than in younger infants (same source).
- That trial's post hoc analysis reported 66.2% seroconversion for YF in children who received simultaneous YF and MMR vaccines, versus 82.6% without MMR (same source). This is relevant to Group 7, though the analysis was post hoc and small.
- A 2026 Lancet trial in infants found 99% seroconversion for the standard dose (PRNT50, 177 of 179) (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0140673625020690). The assay differs from the trial's MN assay.
- Ghanaian infants immunized at 9 months had 98% seroconversion (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2566698/). Sample size and assay are not in the excerpt.
- The comparator appears hard to beat in adults (about 99%). Pediatric benchmarks vary widely (about 85% to 99%), so the trial's 5-point margin could be sensitive to population and timing.

**4. Sponsor statements on design, powering, or delays**
- Sanofi listed yellow fever among new phase 3 programs in its Q4/FY 2025 results (https://www.sanofi.com/assets/dotcom/content-app/events/quaterly-results/2026/2025-q4-and-full-year-2025-results/2026_01_29_Sanofi_Q4FY_2025_Results.pdf).
- I found no public statement on powering, interim analyses, enrollment problems, or design changes for VYF04. The record lists 2,440 planned, with an estimated enrollment type.

**Forecasting notes**
- Adult data support noninferiority with high seroconversion, but the pediatric comparator is less certain. Infant seroconversion for live YF vaccines has ranged widely across studies.
- The record's planned primary completion is 2026-11-28, so a readout may not appear soon.

RESULT ALREADY PUBLIC: Both Part 1 dual primaries (PFS and OS) and the Part 2 PFS primary have been reported as positive, though the registry record does not show results. Part 1 PFS was met at the first interim analysis, and OS at the second (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.54-0.89, P = 0.0020 in the overall population; [Annals of Oncology](https://www.annalsofoncology.org/article/S0923-7534(24)00721-X/fulltext)). Part 2 PFS was 14.5 months with dostarlimab-niraparib versus 8.3 months with chemotherapy alone (HR 0.60; 95% CI 0.43-0.82; P=.0007) ([Cancer Therapy Advisor, SGO 2024](https://www.cancertherapyadvisor.com/reports/dostarlimab-niraparib-pfs-endometrial-cancer/)).

**Part 1 details**
- The PFS primary showed HR 0.64 (95% CI 0.51 to 0.80; P<0.001) in the overall population ([NEJM abstract via PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36972026/)).
- OS was tested at 51% maturity, with the prespecified P value stopping boundary for the log-rank test crossed (P = 0.01101) ([Annals of Oncology](https://www.annalsofoncology.org/article/S0923-7534(24)00721-X/fulltext)).
- OS in the pMMR subgroup was not significant: HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.60-1.04, nominal P=0.0493, with the dMMR HR at 0.32 ([ScienceDirect](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092375342400721X)).
- Four-year dMMR update (ASCO 2026, [Gynecologic Oncology](https://www.gynecologiconcology-online.net/article/S0090-8258(26)01985-2/fulltext)): OS HR 0.34 (95% CI, 0.19-0.63). This is dMMR-only, so it does not bear on the overall-population primary.

**Part 2 details**
- The primary endpoint was PFS in the overall and MMRp/MSS populations; 291 patients were randomized (192 dostar/CP + dostar/nira; 99 PBO/CP) ([ESMO Open abstract](https://www.esmoopen.com/article/S2059-7029(24)01307-3/fulltext)).
- MMRp/MSS PFS HR was 0.63 (95% CI 0.44–0.91) ([ASCO Post](https://ascopost.com/news/march-2024/dostarlimab-based-combinations-in-advanced-endometrial-cancer)). The same ESMO Open abstract says OS follow-up is ongoing.

**Comparator and base rates**
- Carboplatin-paclitaxel is the standard treatment for advanced disease; although effective in nearly 50% of patients, most experience disease progression within a year ([ASCO Post](https://ascopost.com/news/march-2023/ruby-trial-dostarlimab-plus-carboplatin-and-paclitaxel-in-advanced-endometrial-cancer/)).
- Historical median OS is less than 3 years (NEJM, RUBY Part 1 paper, [SGO PDF](https://connected.sgo.org/sites/default/files/course/2023-05/RUBY%20Part%201%20-%20Mirza%20-%20NEJM.pdf)).
- Crossover is high: 173/249 placebo patients (69.5%) received subsequent anticancer therapy ([Annals of Oncology](https://orbi.uliege.be/bitstream/2268/320102/1/ARTICLE%20ANNALS%20ONCOLOGY%20RUBY%202024.pdf)). This dilutes OS.

**Same-mechanism and same-disease trials**
- NRG-GY018 (pembrolizumab, anti-PD-1): median PFS in the pMMR cohort was 13.1 months with pembrolizumab and 8.7 months with placebo (HR 0.54) ([Request PDF](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389590176_Pembrolizumab_plus_chemotherapy_in_advanced_or_recurrent_endometrial_cancer_overall_survival_and_exploratory_analyses_of_the_NRG_GY018_phase_3_randomized_trial)). At about 4 years, OS in the pMMR cohort had an HR of 0.86 (95% CI, 0.69-1.08) ([OncLive](https://www.onclive.com/view/pembrolizumab-plus-chemotherapy-shows-long-term-os-benefit-in-advanced-recurrent-endometrial-cancer)).
- DUO-E (durvalumab, anti-PD-L1): the ITT PFS HR was 0.71 and the pMMR HR was 0.77. Interim OS was not significant for durvalumab alone (HR 0.77, P=.120) ([JCO abstract](https://diposit.ub.edu/dspace/handle/2445/214044)).
- Pattern: PD-(L)1 combinations with chemotherapy have reliably met PFS. The benefit is concentrated in dMMR, and pMMR OS is the weak point.

**Sponsor and investigator statements**
- Enrollment was affected by COVID-19: RUBY Part 1 recruited patients during the coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic, and a smaller number of patients from Europe (n = 136) enrolled ([Annals of Oncology](https://www.annalsofoncology.org/article/S0923-7534(24)00721-X/fulltext)).
- Randomization closed in February 2021, per the NEJM paper ([NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2216334)).
- I found no sponsor statement on powering, design changes, or delays for the current OS or Part 2 follow-up, and no announced final-analysis date.

**RESULT ALREADY PUBLIC:** Not applicable. I found no efficacy result for this trial. The sponsor-linked HOPE-BE baseline paper says the study had not been unblinded, and that efficacy results will come in a future publication ([ERJ Open Research](https://publications.ersnet.org/content/erjor/12/4/00182-2026)). I found no topline press release.

**Earlier trials of this drug (HSK31858/florensocatib)**
- **SAVE-BE (phase 2, China):** 226 patients were randomly assigned, with a 24-week treatment period. The primary endpoint was exacerbation frequency. The incidence rate ratio vs placebo was 0.52 (95% CI 0.34-0.80; p=0.0031) for the 20 mg group and 0.41 (0.26-0.66; p=0.0002) for the 40 mg group ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40154523/)).
- **Limits of SAVE-BE:** No improvement in lung function or quality of life scores was observed ([EurekAlert](https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/1078722)). The trial ran 24 weeks, so the 52-week effect is untested.

**Same mechanism, same disease**
- **Brensocatib (ASPEN, phase 3, n≈1,721):** Rate ratios were 0.79 (adjusted P=0.004) and 0.81 (adjusted P=0.005) for the 10 mg and 25 mg doses ([Insmed](https://investor.insmed.com/2025-04-23-New-England-Journal-of-Medicine-Publishes-Positive-Results-from-Insmeds-Pivotal-Phase-3-ASPEN-Study-of-Brensocatib-in-Patients-with-Bronchiectasis)). FDA approval followed on August 12, 2025 ([ICER](https://icer.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/ICER_NCFB-Final-Report_For-Publication_103025.pdf)).
- **Comparison:** The phase 2 florensocatib effect (~50–60%) is about three times the phase 3 brensocatib effect (~20%). This suggests the small phase 2 estimate may overstate the true effect. A review also notes a ceiling effect for DPP-1 inhibitor efficacy ([ERS review](https://publications.ersnet.org/content/errev/34/176/240257)).
- **Verducatib (BI 1291583):** The therapy is currently being investigated in the Phase III AIRTIVITY (NCT06872892) trial. ([market report](https://www.streetinsider.com/GetNews/Non-Cystic+Fibrosis+Bronchiectasis+Pipeline+Landscape+2026:+Late-Stage+Candidates,+MOA+Trends,+and+ROA+|+Insmed,+AstraZeneca,+Zambon,+CSL+Behring,+Chiesi+Farmaceutici/27255168.html)).

**Other diseases:** I found only preclinical COPD data, with anti-inflammatory activity in animal models ([Frontiers](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/pharmacology/articles/10.3389/fphar.2025.1656316/full)). No human data found.

**Endpoint base rate and comparator:** The comparator is placebo. In ASPEN the placebo arm averaged 1.29 exacerbations per year. I found no systematic count of past bronchiectasis exacerbation trials. A meta-analysis of the DPP-1 trials notes that these trials were relatively small, used different doses and background treatments ([PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12659227/)). One source cites macrolides at about 50% risk reduction as a benchmark, though it is a sponsor-linked press item ([EurekAlert](https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/1078722)).

**Sponsor statements on power, design, and enrollment**
- **Power:** The planned sample of 669 (446 drug, 223 placebo) assumed a one-sided significance level of 0.025, the power of 90%, a negative-binomial dispersion parameter of 1.40, and a 20% dropout rate. The paper does not state the assumed effect size in the sections I reviewed ([ERJ PDF](https://publications.ersnet.org/content/erjor/early/2026/04/02/23120541.00182-2026.full.pdf)).
- **Design:** The HOPE-BE trial has only adopted the higher dose group of florensocatib. The 2:1 randomization was agreed with the regulator (same source).
- **Enrollment:** 700 patients were enrolled from 67 sites in mainland China between September 2024 and November 2025. This exceeds the planned 669, so I found no enrollment trouble. The registry's site count and last-update date are stale.
- **Interim analyses, delays, design changes:** None found.
- **Conflicts:** The statistical team from the sponsor independently conducted statistical analyses. Haisco employees are among the authors ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42639008/)).

**Related registration:** NCT07616375 is an open-label, single-arm safety study for participants who had previously participated in the HSK31858-301 study ([ClinicalTrials.gov](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07616375)).

**Evidence brief: NCT06641466 (rimegepant, perimenstrual prevention)**

**Result status:** No public result found. The registry shows no posted results ([ClinicalTrials.gov record](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06641466)), and I found no sponsor release or publication for this trial.

**Earlier rimegepant data in menstrual migraine (none randomized and placebo-controlled)**
- Rimegepant prevented perimenstrual attacks in 17/20 cycles (85%) in a five-woman case series ([J Headache Pain](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s10194-025-02185-y)). The authors called it hypothesis-generating.
- A retrospective Chinese cohort (n=43, uncontrolled) found attack duration fell by 20.5 h from baseline (p < 0.001) after three cycles ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41928122/)). The authors said the results are associations only.

**Rimegepant in other migraine settings**
- A randomized, placebo-controlled phase 4 episodic-migraine prevention trial (n=692) found both rimegepant 75 mg every other day and rimegepant 75 mg daily were superior to placebo in reducing monthly migraine days over 12 weeks ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43056654)). The phase 3 mean reduction was 1.1 days versus placebo over a 12-week period ([J Headache Pain](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s10194-025-02185-y)).

**Same mechanism in this disease: atogepant (AbbVie LUNA)**
- LUNA used a 7-day cycle-timed regimen, the same design as this trial. Participants took the drug for seven consecutive days starting three days before the onset of menses, repeated over three menstrual cycles. ([Allsci](https://allsci.com/news/clinical-trials/atogepant-menstrual-migraine-abbvies-meets/))
- Result: a mean reduction of 1.20 perimenstrual migraine days versus 0.40 with placebo, yielding a 0.80-day between-group difference (P < .0001) ([NeurologyLive](https://www.neurologylive.com/view/intermittent-atogepant-reduces-perimenstrual-migraine-days-in-phase-3-luna-trial)). The primary was met and all eight ranked secondary endpoints were met ([AbbVie via BioSpace](https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/abbvie-extends-migraine-leadership-with-positive-phase-3-atogepant-results-in-menstrual-migraine)).
- Caveat: the reporting is topline only. Absent numerical results limit appraisal of clinical magnitude.

**Historical menstrual-migraine prevention trials**
- Frovatriptan RCT (n=546): incidence of MAM headache during the 6-day PMP was 67% for placebo, 52% for frovatriptan 2.5 mg QD, and 41% for frovatriptan 2.5 mg BID. The endpoint was incidence, not days ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15277618/)).
- A meta-analysis found that out of 342 studies, 26 RCTs met the criteria. Prevention endpoints varied across trials ([J Headache Pain](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s10194-024-01848-6)).
- Comparator: the record's "Standard of Care" arm is acute-as-needed treatment, not a preventive. The placebo arm is the relevant benchmark. In LUNA, placebo fell by 0.40 days.

**Sponsor statements on powering, interims, enrollment, delays**
- I found nothing from Pfizer or investigators on powering, interim analyses, enrollment problems, or design changes.
- The record shows no data monitoring committee, 723 estimated enrollment, and a planned primary completion of 2026-11-29 while still listed as recruiting ([record](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06641466)). Check current status, since these dates look inconsistent.

**Flags for the forecaster**
- The primary outcome is change from the observation period, not explicitly a placebo-adjusted contrast. Check the statistical analysis plan if available.
- The design is labeled single-group but has four arms, including a randomized placebo.

**Evidence brief: NCT06954961 (D-0502, taragarestrant, vs fulvestrant)**

**Result status:** No result found. The sponsor's August 2026 interim report still describes the registrational Phase III as ongoing ([HKEX filing](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/app/sehk/2026/108806/documents/sehk26082101888.pdf)).

**Earlier trials of this drug**
- No randomized efficacy data for D-0502 were found. Phase I parts reportedly met their endpoints in 2021–2023 ([HKEX filing](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/app/sehk/2026/108806/documents/sehk26082101888.pdf)).
- A review reports single-agent Phase I data with good tolerability, and ORRs of 15% when combined with palbociclib ([Annual Review](https://www.annualreviews.org/content/journals/10.1146/annurev-med-052423-122001?crawler=true&mimetype=application%2Fpdf)). I found no p-values or sample sizes.
- Preclinical claims of superior potency over fulvestrant come from xenograft work ([AACR 2018](https://cancerres.aacrjournals.org/content/78/13_Supplement/5776)).

**Other oral SERDs, same mechanism, same disease**
- Elacestrant (EMERALD, post-CDK4/6i): overall PFS 2.8 vs 1.9 months; ESR1-mutant 3.8 vs 1.9 months ([JCO](https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/JCO.22.00338)). Overall HR was 0.70 in the earlier SABCS-era report ([MDPI review](https://www.mdpi.com/2072-6694/16/3/619)). The non-ESR1 subgroup HR was 0.86, so benefit was concentrated in ESR1-mutant disease ([manufacturer site](https://www.orserduhcp.com/efficacy/)).
- Imlunestrant (EMBER-3): overall HR 0.87, P = .12, not significant. ESR1-mutant HR 0.62 ([Targeted Oncology](https://www.targetedonc.com/view/imlunestrant-improves-pfs-in-esr1-mutant-advanced-breast-cancer)).
- Giredestrant (acelERA) did not show superiority over endocrine therapy overall ([Annual Review](https://www.annualreviews.org/content/journals/10.1146/annurev-med-052423-122001?crawler=true&mimetype=application%2Fpdf)).
- Pooled across 8 oral SERD RCTs (n=3,978), PFS did not differ significantly from standard therapy: HR 0.80 (0.62–1.04) ([Cancer Treatment Reviews, 2026](https://www.cancertreatmentreviews.com/article/S0305-7372(26)00007-1/fulltext)).

**Comparator and endpoint base rates**
- Fulvestrant 250 mg is the standard comparator. In CONFIRM, 500 mg beat 250 mg on PFS (HR 0.80, P = .006) ([JCO](https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/JCO.2010.28.8415)). This trial uses the 500 mg-type monthly schedule with a loading dose ([record](https://www.drugs.com/pro/fulvestrant-injection.html)); the record's dosing description is not explicit on dose, so check the protocol.
- Fulvestrant after CDK4/6 inhibitors shows minimal efficacy, with median PFS of 3–4 months in ESR1-mutant disease ([MDPI review](https://www.mdpi.com/2072-6694/16/3/619)). This is a weak comparator, which favors a PFS win for a new agent.
- I did not find a published base rate for PFS-primary Chinese SERD trials specifically.

**Sponsor statements**
- Dec 2025: the trial was "proceeding as planned" and was designed as a head-to-head comparison ([Alphamab release](https://www.alphamabonc.com/en/html/news/2746.html)).
- Aug 2026: the Phase III is described as ongoing. The sponsor gave no interim, powering, or enrollment details that I could find.
- The record lists no DMC, and the planned primary completion (2026-11-30) is about a week away. I found no public statement on delays or design changes.

**Gaps:** No powering assumptions, interim analysis plans, enrollment problems, or design amendments were found. Peer-reviewed D-0502 clinical data were not found.

**Evidence brief: NCT07672561 (WD-890, moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis)**

**No result is public.** I found no topline, conference, or press release for this trial, and the registry still lists it as recruiting.

**1. Prior WD-890 data**
- The only efficacy data I found are preclinical. In an IL-23-induced mouse psoriasis model, the levels of IL-17 and IFN-γ in serum were obviously dropped in the groups treated with WD-890 ([ScienceDirect, 2023](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0753332223014099)). No human effect sizes, p-values, or sample sizes were found.
- A separate dose-response Phase 2 study of WD-890 in the same disease, with the same Week 16 endpoint, is NCT06912165 ([Medpath](https://trial.medpath.com/clinical-trial/e2a608e4e57bfbd5/nct06912165-wd-890-tablets-plaque-psoriasis)). I found no posted results for it.
- The sponsor's own pipeline page calls WD-890 a Phase II asset ([Wenda pipeline](http://www.wendapharma.com/pipeline.php)). A later sponsor-linked profile says it has entered Phase III clinical trials ([Synapse](https://synapse.patsnap.com/organization/538aaac4cb0c4551cbaf780d5db6f428)).

**2. Same mechanism and same disease**
- Deucravacitinib, the approved TYK2 inhibitor, reached PASI-75 (58.4% vs. 35.1%) against apremilast at week 16 in Phase 3 ([Frontiers network meta-analysis](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2023.1180170/full)). That meta-analysis also found that low-dose groups of oral TYK2 and PDE4 inhibitors did not exhibit superior efficacy to placebo.
- Zasocitinib, a newer TYK2 inhibitor, met its co-primary endpoints in two Phase 3 trials. Its sPGA 0 rate was 39.9% and 33.7% ... versus placebo (0.7% and 1.4%) ([Takeda](https://www.takeda.com/newsroom/newsreleases/2026/zasocitinib-phase3-clinical-trial-results/)).
- Other oral agents in China: prifemilast reached PASI 75 ... 51.8% (88/170) ... and 57.4% (97/169) ... compared with 10.8% (18/166) for placebo at week 16 ([HCPLive](https://www.hcplive.com/view/prifemilast-achieves-pasi-75-up-to-57-patients-psoriasis)).

**3. Endpoint base rates**
- Placebo PASI 75 at week 16 has run about 11–13% in the comparators I found: prifemilast 10.8%, tofacitinib 12.5% in Asian patients ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28558978)), and ropsacitinib 13.3% ([Frontiers](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2023.1180170/full)). Beating placebo is the low bar here.
- Apremilast is the harder benchmark. The study has no active comparator, so it does not test that bar.
- I found no published success rate for Phase 3 psoriasis trials. One industry report counts 255 small-molecule trials run in plaque psoriasis in Phase 3, but it gives no outcome rates ([AppliedXL](https://www.appliedxl.com/news/newsoara-hpp737-psoriasis-phase3-nct07712705)).

**4. Sponsor and investigator statements**
- I found no statements on powering, interim analyses, enrollment problems, design changes, or delays for this trial.

**5. Record issues to check**
- The planned primary completion date is 2026-11-30, yet the study is still recruiting and started 2026-03-18. With a 16-week primary endpoint, the last participant would need to enroll by about mid-August 2026 for that date to hold. The date and the 375 estimated enrollment may be stale.
- The eligibility age ceiling here is 75. The Phase 2 sister study lists 70 ([CenterWatch](https://www.centerwatch.com/clinical-trials/listings/NCT06912165/a-study-of-wd-890-in-participants-with-moderate-to-severe-plaque-psoriasis)).

**RESULT ALREADY PUBLIC:** The primary PFS result is out. By blinded independent central review, median PFS was 11.1 vs 4.4 months (HR 0.39, 95% CI 0.30–0.51, nominal p<0.0001) in 365 patients randomized 1:1. Source: the JCO paper, <https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42727044>, and an ASCO Post summary, <https://ascopost.com/news/september-2026/phase-iii-trial-compares-her2-directed-antibody-drug-conjugates-in-advanced-breast-cancer/>. The record links to this paper: the NCT06968585 page lists it as a publication. The match rests on the same sponsor, 365 patients, and a July 2023 start. The record is last updated May 2026 and still shows "active, not recruiting."

**Earlier trials of this drug (same disease)**
- Phase 1 dose expansion (single arm, 58 patients): ORR 73.9% at 4.8 mg/kg (n=23) and median PFS 12.3 months. No p-value. <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11700426/>
- Phase 1 grade ≥3 corneal epitheliopathy was 30.9%. <https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365040219_Phase_I_Study_of_A166_a_Novel_Antibody-Drug_Conjugate_in_Advanced_HER2-expressing_Solid_Tumors>
- I found no other pre-phase 3 trials with a PFS endpoint.

**Phase 3 details (from the published result)**
- ORR by BICR was 76.9% vs 53.0%, with median DoR 12.2 vs 5.7 months. <https://ascopost.com/news/september-2026/phase-iii-trial-compares-her2-directed-antibody-drug-conjugates-in-advanced-breast-cancer/>
- PFS benefit held across prior-line subgroups (HR 0.36 for one prior line, 0.39 for ≥2). <https://www.annalsofoncology.org/article/S0923-7534(25)04803-3/pdf>
- OS was immature, HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.38–1.03). OS is secondary, so this is not a test of the primary endpoint. <https://ascopost.com/news/september-2026/phase-iii-trial-compares-her2-directed-antibody-drug-conjugates-in-advanced-breast-cancer/>
- Ocular events were the main toxicity; grade ≥3 TEAEs were 69.8% vs 63.7%. <https://www.annalsofoncology.org/article/S0923-7534(25)04803-3/pdf>

**Comparator benchmark**
- T-DM1 performed far below its historical benchmark. In EMILIA, median PFS for T-DM1 was 9.6 months. <https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1209124> Here the T-DM1 arm had 4.4 months. A likely reason is that 55.9% of patients had prior pyrotinib. <https://www.emjreviews.com/oncology/symposium/recent-advances-in-the-treatment-of-early-stage-her2-positive-breast-cancer-updates-from-esmo-2025-s330425/>
- A same-setting HER2 ADC with a different payload, T-DXd, achieved 12-month PFS of 75.8% vs 34.1% for T-DM1 in DESTINY-Breast03. <https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2115022>

**Sponsor statements, design, and delays**
- The sponsor reported a pre-specified interim analysis for the PFS result. <https://www.biopharmaapac.com/news/136/7048/sichuan-kelun-biotechs-trastuzumab-botidotin-approved-in-china-for-her2-positive-metastatic-breast-cancer.html>
- Enrollment ran July 2023 to April 2024 at 57 Chinese centers. <https://ascopost.com/news/september-2026/phase-iii-trial-compares-her2-directed-antibody-drug-conjugates-in-advanced-breast-cancer/>
- NMPA approved the drug on October 17, 2025 on this trial's basis. <https://pharmacally.com/trastuzumab-botidotin-a166-phase-3-her2-positive-breast-cancer/>
- I found no reports of powering assumptions, enrollment trouble, design changes, or delays.

**Bottom line for the forecaster:** The published result shows the primary endpoint was met, with a large effect. If the record's endpoint is the same BICR PFS, a forecast should reflect that outcome. The main uncertainty is whether the record and the publication describe the same trial. The matching sponsor, enrollment, and dates suggest they do.

**RESULT ALREADY PUBLIC:** No. Enrollment closed October 2, 2026, with over 20 U.S. sites participating ([PR Newswire, Oct 8 2026](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/saol-therapeutics-announces-completion-of-enrollment-in-pivotal-phase-iii-beacon-trial-of-sl1002-for-the-treatment-of-chronic-pain-related-to-osteoarthritis-of-the-knee-302901305.html)). Topline results are expected in the second quarter of 2027, which conflicts with the record's 2026-11-30 primary completion date.

**Earlier SL1002 trials in knee OA**
- Phase II COMPASS (NCT05470608) enrolled 132 patients on a 3:1 randomized design, with the efficacy measure average pain intensity at 3 months (12 weeks) versus placebo ([Saol PR, 2022](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/saol-therapeutics-announces-first-patient-enrolled-in-phase-2-compass-trial-evaluating-the-safety-and-efficacy-profile-of-sl-1002-for-treatment-of-knee-pain-associated-with-osteoarthritis-301602027.html)). Topline was originally guided for the first quarter of 2024 ([Saol PR, 2023](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/saol-therapeutics-announces-completion-of-enrollment-in-both-the-phase-ii-compass-osteoarthritis-knee-pain-trial-and-the-phase-ii-raise-limb-spasticity-trial-301930918.html)). I found no published COMPASS results, effect size, or p-value. Treat efficacy as unknown.
- Phase III investigators overlap heavily: nearly all our investigators from the Phase II COMPASS Trial returned. This shows continuity, not efficacy.

**Same mechanism elsewhere (uncertain)**
- The sponsor calls SL1002 a novel, chemoneurolytic injection. I found no agent identity, so don't assume it is phenol.
- Phenol genicular neurolysis: an open-label cohort of forty-three patients showed mean pain falling from 7.2 to 4.2 at 6 months ([Risso, Pain Pract 2021](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33277760/)). Without a control arm, this is weak evidence.
- A scoping review found that all studies demonstrated that chemical neurolysis resulted in improved pain or functional outcomes ([Pain Medicine](https://doi.org/10.1093/pm/pnae109)). These were mostly uncontrolled.
- A phenol pilot with a placebo arm exists (NCT04989660), but I found no results.

**SL1002 in another disease**
- In spasticity, the Phase II RAISE trial reported a decrease of -1.18 versus -0.33 in the vehicle group on the Modified Ashworth Score at six months ([Synapse summary](https://synapse.patsnap.com/article/saol-therapeutics-reports-positive-results-from-sl-1002-spasticity-trial)). That trial's primary endpoint was overall safety, and the outcome is not pain, so it says little about OA pain.

**Placebo response and base rates**
- A 2026 meta-analysis of 179 non-surgical knee OA trials found that a Hedges' g of 0.5 or greater was seen in the placebo arm of 60% of trials ([Holtedahl et al., Osteoarthritis Cartilage Open](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42657310/)). Trials conducted in North America reported the highest effect sizes. This is a U.S.-only trial.
- Saline placebo injections produce strong responses: in one meta-analysis, responder rates exceeded 50% at 1-, 3-, and 6-months. ([EFORT Open Reviews](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12495556/)).
- I did not find a published success rate for NRS-primary Phase III knee OA trials. A secondary source attributes high late-stage failure in this indication to placebo response ([Cognivia](https://cognivia.com/the-placebo-response-in-drug-development-part-2-osteoarthritis/)).

**Sponsor statements**
- The company plans to initiate an additional Phase III study in its knee pain program to support a planned regulatory filing. This suggests the sponsor may expect to need more evidence than this trial alone.
- I found nothing on powering, interim analyses, enrollment problems (enrollment is complete), or design changes.
- The record's primary endpoint is the weekly mean of pain while walking, while the Phase II endpoint was average pain intensity. Confirm whether this is a change.

**Status:** No topline result for NCT07010471 (EMERALD) is public as of 22 Nov 2026. The company guides to a Q4 2026 readout, and recruitment is complete ([SEC Q1 2026 release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1689548/000168954826000049/praxisq12026pr.htm)). The Q3 2026 release says the study is in its final stages ([SEC Q3 2026 release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1689548/000168954826000086/praxisq32026pr.htm)).

**Prior trial, same drug (EMBOLD, NCT05818553; SCN2A/SCN8A only)**

I found no p-value for this cohort.
- The registrational cohort (n=51) reported a 53% placebo-adjusted reduction (p<0.0002) and a 66% increase in motor seizure-free days (p=0.034) ([Praxis AES wrap, Dec 2025](https://investors.praxismedicines.com/news-releases/news-release-details/praxis-aes-wrap-best-class-potential-across-rare-pediatric-and)).
