- The FDA NDA for SCN2A/SCN8A has a PDUFA date of 27 Dec 2026 ([SEC Q3 2026 release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1689548/000168954826000086/praxisq32026pr.htm)). That review rests on EMBOLD, not EMERALD.

**Other diseases and other drugs**
- Same sponsor, sodium-channel drug in focal seizures (vormatrigine, POWER1): the primary endpoint was missed, though a responder-rate secondary was met ([Praxis Q3 2026 context](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1689548/000168954826000086/praxisq32026pr.htm); [Synapse summary](https://synapse.patsnap.com/drug/8d0e18c3fb294f5c895f141a7d39287a)).
- Elsunersen (ASO, SCN2A-DEE, different mechanism): Part A showed a 77% placebo-adjusted monthly seizure reduction ([SEC Q1 2026 release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1689548/000168954826000049/praxisq12026pr.htm)).
- I found no data on relutrigine in other DEE genotypes or on other sodium-channel drugs in broad DEE.

**Base rates and comparator**
- I found no published rate of primary-endpoint success for DEE add-on trials, and no data on placebo response in this population. Treat this as a gap.

**Sponsor statements on design and enrollment**
- The company said recruitment for EMERALD is complete ([SEC Q1 2026 release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1689548/000168954826000049/praxisq12026pr.htm)). A secondary summary puts enrollment near 200 against a 160 target ([Synapse](https://synapse.patsnap.com/drug/8d0e18c3fb294f5c895f141a7d39287a)). I could not verify this against a primary source.
- I found no statements on EMERALD powering, interim analyses, or delays.
- Relevant context: the sponsor's ulixacaltamide Phase 3 was stopped for futility at an interim analysis in 2025, which the CEO called a surprise ([Praxis, Feb 2025](https://ir.praxismedicines.com/news-releases/news-release-details/praxis-precision-medicines-provides-update-essential3-and)). This is a different drug and disease.

**Forecasting caveats**
- EMBOLD's effect was seen in a genetically narrow, small population. EMERALD is broad and heterogeneous, and one analyst flags that effect size may shrink ([BioCosm](https://biocosm.io/drug/pipeline-prax-562)). That is commentary, not data.
- EMBOLD's endpoint matches EMERALD's primary endpoint ([NeurologyLive](https://www.neurologylive.com/view/breakthrough-therapy-designation-granted-relutrigine-scn2a-scn8a-developmental-epileptic-encephalopathies)).

**RESULT ALREADY PUBLIC:** No. I found no announced result for NCT04969731. The record was last updated in 2021, so its status may be stale.

**Sponsor and investigator statements**
- I found no public statement on powering, interim analyses, enrollment problems, or design changes. The record says a data monitoring committee exists, but I found no details of its rules.
- Trial registry-linked literature lists two GC Cell employees as co-authors of a preclinical paper, which is a conflict to weigh. [pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37078953](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37078953/)

**Earlier trials in pancreatic cancer**
- No randomized clinical data for Immuncell-LC in pancreatic cancer surfaced. A mouse adjuvant-model study found longer recurrence-free survival with CIK plus gemcitabine than with control (median 54 days, P=0.013), but overall survival did not differ. [pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37078953](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37078953/)
- A single-arm phase 2 trial in gemcitabine-refractory advanced disease exists, but I found no results posted. [ichgcp.net/clinical-trials-registry/NCT00965718](https://ichgcp.net/clinical-trials-registry/NCT00965718)
- A retrospective, non-randomized advanced-pancreatic study reported median overall survival of 13.5 versus 6.6 months with CIK-based therapy, and its authors flagged the selection bias. [link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13045-016-0237-6](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13045-016-0237-6)

**Same drug in other diseases**
- Adjuvant Immuncell-LC in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the strongest evidence. In a 230-patient randomized trial, median recurrence-free survival was 44 versus 30 months. [koreabiomed.com (idxno=26521)](https://www.koreabiomed.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=26521)
- At nine years, overall survival was 64% versus 56.3%, not statistically significant. [koreabiomed.com (idxno=26521)](https://www.koreabiomed.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=26521)
- A 2026 retrospective liver-transplant study reported 24-month recurrence-free survival of 87.5% versus 62.9%. It was not randomized. [koreabiomed.com (idxno=33148)](https://www.koreabiomed.com/news/articleViewAmp.html?idxno=33148)

**Other drugs with the same mechanism in this disease**
- A randomized phase 2 adjuvant immunotherapy trial (GI-4000 plus gemcitabine) did not meet its recurrence-free survival endpoint. [mdpi.com/3258352](https://www.mdpi.com/3258352)
- A 2025 review judged that most immune-based adjuvant attempts in pancreatic cancer have failed to show clinical success. [mdpi.com/2072-6694/17/7/1246](https://www.mdpi.com/2072-6694/17/7/1246)

**Base rates and the comparator**
- Gemcitabine is an established comparator. In CONKO-001, adjuvant gemcitabine versus observation produced median disease-free survival of 13.4 versus 6.7 months. [pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24104372](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24104372/)
- Adding erlotinib or sorafenib to adjuvant gemcitabine did not improve survival in CONKO-005 or CONKO-006. [tgh.amegroups.org/article/view/5029/html](https://tgh.amegroups.org/article/view/5029/html)
- Later trials found gemcitabine plus capecitabine (ESPAC-4) and mFOLFIRINOX (PRODIGE-24) superior to gemcitabine alone, so a gemcitabine-only control is an older standard. [hemeoncbuddy.org/trials/conko-001](https://hemeoncbuddy.org/trials/conko-001/) (secondary summary)
- I did not find a clean historical hit rate for recurrence-free survival endpoints in resected pancreatic cancer.

**Bottom line for the forecaster:** The only randomized efficacy signal for this drug is in HCC, using the same endpoint type. Pancreatic evidence is preclinical or non-randomized. Adjuvant immunotherapy in pancreatic cancer has a poor track record, and the record's 2026-12 primary completion has no public result yet.

**Evidence brief: NCT06842823 (ALPHA-ORBIT, navenibart, HAE)**

No topline result is public. The 6-month endpoint is not yet reported.

**Timing and sponsor statements**
- Enrollment finished in June 2026. Patient enrollment in ALPHA-ORBIT was completed in June. [BioCryst, Aug 2026](https://ir.biocryst.com/news-releases/news-release-details/biocryst-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results)
- Topline data are now guided to Q3 2027, covering both 6- and 12-month endpoints. Earlier guidance was early 2027. [Astria, Nov 2025](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251112064626/en/Astria-Therapeutics-Reports-Third-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results-and-Provides-a-Corporate-Update). The registry's 2026-12 primary completion date looks stale.
- The sponsor said the trial was up to 145 patients, with the primary analysis at 6 months. [Astria, Jan 2025](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1454789/000110465925002872/tm253046d1_ex99-1.htm)
- The sponsor described the adolescent arm as open-label. [Astria, Feb 2025](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250227320197/en/Astria-Therapeutics-Initiates-ALPHA-ORBIT-Phase-3-Pivotal-Trial-of-Navenibart-in-Hereditary-Angioedema) So the placebo comparison is effectively adults only.
- I found no interim-analysis, power, or effect-size assumption statements in my searches.
- Astria was acquired by BioCryst in January 2026. [Pharmaletter](https://www.thepharmaletter.com/ones-to-watch/biocryst-pharmaceuticals)

**Earlier navenibart data (all uncontrolled, no placebo)**
- Phase 1b/2 ALPHA-STAR, n=16: reduction in mean monthly attack rate of 90-95% and up to a 67% attack-free rate over 6 months. I found no p-values. [Astria, Feb 2025](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250227320197/en/Astria-Therapeutics-Initiates-ALPHA-ORBIT-Phase-3-Pivotal-Trial-of-Navenibart-in-Hereditary-Angioedema)
- With 29 patients, the reduction was 84–92% mean and 93-100% median. [Astria, Nov 2025](https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/astria-therapeutics-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-results-and-provides-a-corporate-update)
- Long-term open-label ALPHA-SOLAR: 92% and 90% mean attack reductions in the 3-month and the 6-month dosing regimens. [BioCryst Q1 2026 call](https://finance.yahoo.com/sectors/healthcare/articles/biocryst-bcrx-q1-2026-earnings-191137702.html)
- Other diseases: nothing found.

**Same-disease comparators (placebo-controlled)**
- Lanadelumab (HELP, kallikrein): reduced mean attack rates by up to 87% versus placebo. [Angioedema News](https://angioedemanews.com/professional/preventing-hae-attacks-current-and-emerging-therapeutic-approaches/)
- Garadacimab (VANGUARD, FXIIa): 0.27 vs 2.01 attacks/month, P < .0001. [Healio](https://www.healio.com/clinical-guidance/hereditary-angioedema/long-term-prophylaxis-treatment-options)
- Donidalorsen (OASIS-HAE, prekallikrein ASO): Q4W: 81%; Q8W: 55% reductions vs placebo over weeks 0–24. [Penn State review](https://pure.psu.edu/en/publications/donidalorsen-for-the-treatment-of-hereditary-angioedema-a-review-/)
- Berotralstat (APeX-2, oral kallikrein inhibitor): a mean reduction in attacks of 44% compared with placebo. [Angioedema News](https://angioedemanews.com/professional/preventing-hae-attacks-current-and-emerging-therapeutic-approaches/)
- Pattern: every placebo-controlled HAE prophylaxis trial I found met its attack-rate primary endpoint. I found no systematic success-rate tally for this disease.
- The comparators are not hard to beat. Placebo arms ran about 2.0–2.3 attacks/month, so the bar is effect size rather than beating an active control.

**Caveats**
- ALPHA-STAR reductions are against each patient's own baseline, not placebo, so they cannot be compared directly with placebo-controlled effect sizes.
- A 12-month blinded period means final patients finish in June 2027, which is consistent with the Q3 2027 guidance.

**RESULT ALREADY PUBLIC:** Not applicable. I found no announced result for NCT06382129 (PANKU-Lung02). The sponsor's sister trial, PANKU-Lung01, is a different population (EGFR-mutant) and is covered below.

**1. Earlier BL-B01D1 data in EGFR-wild-type NSCLC (all single-arm, no p-values)**
- Phase 1 expansion: ORR was 44.9% (95% CI, 30.7%-59.8%) for EGFR wild-type NSCLC (n = 49) with DCR 91.8% (https://www.onclive.com/view/bl-b01d1-demonstrates-antitumor-activity-in-egfr-nsclc-and-other-solid-tumors).
- A separate ESMO 2023 report of the NSCLC cohort gave a lower figure: ORR of 30.6% in 62 patients with EGFR wildtype (https://deceraclinical.com/education/activity/ecase/776138A5-6A7D-4C66-9E8A-EDE3D912D9B5/2). The two cuts disagree.
- The same drug (then called SI-B001) plus docetaxel after anti-PD-1/PD-L1 and platinum: 42 patients; ORR of 31.0%, a DCR of 71.4%, and a median DoR of 4.2 months (same source). This is the closest analogue to this trial's population.
- I found no randomized EGFR-wild-type data.

**2. Same drug in other diseases (randomized Phase 3, OS-positive)**
- PANKU-Breast02 (TNBC, interim): median OS was 15.9 months with iza-bren vs. 12.5 months with TPC (HR: 0.60; 95% CI: 0.42-0.85; p=0.0019) (https://news.bms.com/news/corporate-financial/2026/Izalontamab-Brengitecan-Iza-Bren-Demonstrates-Statistically-Significant-and-Clinically-Meaningful-Improvements-in-Overall-Survival-and-Progression-Free-Survival-in-Patients-with-Triple-Negative-Breast-Cancer-and-Esophageal-Squamous-Cell-Carcinoma/default.aspx).
- PANKU-Breast01 (HR+ breast): HR 0.41 for PFS versus chemotherapy (https://trial.medpath.com/drug/4292ea82fc8702ca/izalontamab-brengitecan; aggregator, primary source not checked).

**3. Same drug in EGFR-mutant NSCLC (closest Phase 3 readout, different population)**
- PANKU-Lung01 interim: met its primary endpoint of PFS at a prespecified interim analysis, announced August 2026 (https://www.morningglorysciences.com/en/iza-bren-panku-lung01-phase3-pfs-2026-en/). The same source reports that for OS the filing states only that a trend toward benefit was observed. The reported median PFS was 11.1 vs 5.7 months, HR 0.40 (MedPath, above).

**4. Same mechanism and the comparator**
- HER3-DXd (HERTHENA-Lung02): PFS was improved but OS versus chemotherapy was not (median 16.0 vs. 15.9 months; HR 0.98) (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/400130981_Izalontamab_brengitecan_Iza-bren_BL-B01D1_a_first-in-class_EGFR-HER3_bispecific_antibody-drug_conjugate_for_patients_with_EGFR-mutated_NSCLC_Pooled_analysis_of_phase_1_and_phase_2_trials).
- Docetaxel comparator, TROPION-Lung01 (Dato-DXd vs docetaxel): median OS was 12.9 vs 11.8 months (HR, 0.94; P = .530) (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39250535/). In the nonsquamous subgroup, OS was numerically better, HR 0.84 (https://www.jto.org/article/S1556-0864(24)00922-5/fulltext). Docetaxel response in the nonsquamous arm was 12.8% (https://www.iaslc.org/iaslc-news/press-release/datopotamab-deruxtecan-does-not-meet-its-secondary-primary-endpoint).
- Docetaxel is hard to beat on OS in this setting. Investigators in that trial said patients only survive for about one year (https://www.astrazeneca.com/media-centre/press-releases/2024/dato-dxd-showed-median-overall-survival-of-146-months-in-patients-with-advanced-nsclc-in-tropion-lung01-phase-iii-trial.html).

**5. Base rate for OS-primary trials here**
- The main precedent is OS failure after PFS success: TROPION-Lung01 and HERTHENA-Lung02 (above). I found no broader tally of how often trials in this disease meet OS.

**6. Sponsor statements on powering, interims, enrollment, or delays**
- None found for NCT06382129. The sponsor's PANKU-Lung01 used a prespecified interim analysis reviewed by an independent committee (https://www.morningglorysciences.com/en/iza-bren-panku-lung01-phase3-pfs-2026-en/). The record says no DMC for this trial. I could not confirm whether an interim is planned here.

**Bottom line:** Phase 1 data suggest activity in EGFR-wild-type disease, but there is no randomized evidence. The docetaxel comparator is weak. OS is the sole primary endpoint, and the closest analogues show PFS gains that did not translate into OS. Sponsor statements are sparse.

**Evidence brief: NCT06361537 (OCTA-C1-INH, acute HAE attack, time to relief)**

**Result status:** No public result found. Searches turned up no Octapharma press release or publication for this trial. The [ClinicalTrials.gov record](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06361537) was last updated in August 2026, and I found no sponsor statement on interim analyses, powering, or delays.

**Prior trials of the same drug:** None found in the registry search. The only human data on OCTA-C1-INH were a [single-arm PK study](https://www.scienceopen.com/document/read?vid=be19d187-fb61-4c2a-9fdc-3e8833d9d92c) in attack-free adults. Its n=20 and mean total dose of 1457.3 (356.51) IU say nothing about efficacy. Its half-life was 74.1 (19) hours when determined using C1-INH activity.

**Same mechanism, same disease (plasma-derived C1-INH):**
- Berinert IMPACT-1 (n=124–125, placebo-controlled, same 20 IU/kg dose): median time to onset of relief was significantly shorter with C1 esterase inhibitor concentrate at a dose of 20 U/kg than with placebo (0.5 vs 1.5 hours; P = .0025). The 10 U/kg arm was not significant (p=0.273). Source: [Craig 2009](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19767078/), [FDA label](https://www.fda.gov/media/77803/download).
- Berinert placebo response: onset of relief was experienced within 4 hours by 69.8% of BERINERT treatment group and 42.9% of placebo group. Source: [Berinert label](https://www.berinert.com/professional/efficacy-safety).
- Nanofiltered Cinryze (n=68, same endpoint family): median time to the onset of unequivocal relief from an attack was 2 hours in the subjects treated with C1 inhibitor concentrate but longer than 4 hours in those given placebo (P=0.02). Source: [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa0805538).
- Recombinant C1-INH (Ruconest, n=75): median 90 vs 152 minutes to symptom relief. Source: [Angioedema News](https://angioedemanews.com/rhc1inh-ruconest/).
- Timing matters: in IMPACT-1, treatment under 6 hours gave considerably shorter times to onset of symptom relief (HR, 3.36) versus placebo, and benefit was smaller after 6 hours. Source: [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23987198/).

**Other diseases / other mechanisms:** Not searched in depth. Ecallantide (placebo-controlled, n≈ a few hundred across EDEMA trials) reached initial improvement at 4 h in 69% compared with 50% treated with placebo. Source: [consensus review](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5857575/).

**Is the comparator hard to beat?** Placebo is the comparator, so this is not an active-control problem. Placebo responses in these trials were slow and variable. Head-to-head trials among acute agents are lacking. Source: [Medicaid NV monograph](https://www.medicaid.nv.gov/Downloads/provider/Hereditary_Angioedema_Agents_2021-04.pdf).

**Base rate:** Every placebo-controlled acute-attack C1-INH trial I found met its time-to-relief endpoint. I found no failed trials of this class, though the sample is small and publication-biased.

**Endpoint caveat:** This trial's primary endpoint requires three consecutive "unequivocal" relief ratings, which is stricter than the simpler onset-of-relief definitions in the legacy trials. Its 4-hour window is also the same. Expect a somewhat later median than the legacy trials if the definition is applied strictly.

**Timeline signals:** The trial is still recruiting with a planned primary completion of 2026-12, per the record. A third-party mirror said the study was estimated to conclude by December 31, 2025, which suggests slippage. Source: [clinicaltrials.eu](https://clinicaltrials.eu/trial/study-on-c1-esterase-inhibitor-for-treating-and-preventing-hereditary-angioedema-attacks-in-patients-with-c1-inh-deficiency/).

**Bottom line:** The mechanism and endpoint family have a strong placebo-controlled track record. The main uncertainties are product-specific efficacy (no prior efficacy data for OCTA-C1-INH), the stricter endpoint definition, and enrollment and timeline slippage.

**Evidence brief: NCT06269705 (ZILRETTA, glenohumeral OA, primary endpoint Week 12 pain vs saline)**

**Result status:** No result found. Pacira's most recent statements say topline data are expected by year-end 2026. The shoulder study completed enrollment in April 2026, per the [Q1 2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1396814/000162828026028854/pcrx-03312026x991.htm), which also said ZILRETTA could become the first on-label shoulder OA product if the study succeeds.

**Earlier ZILRETTA trials in this disease**
- No shoulder efficacy data found. The only shoulder study located is a [Phase 2 open-label PK and safety study](https://www.biospace.com/flexion-therapeutics-announces-publication-of-results-from-phase-2-pharmacokinetics-pk-and-safety-study-of-zilretta-in-shoulder-osteoarthritis-oa) of 25 patients, which reported PK and safety similar to knee Phase 3 studies.
- Knee pivotal ([FDA review](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2017/208845Orig1s000StatR.pdf)): primary endpoint (average daily pain at Week 12 vs placebo) was met, p<0.0001. The second comparison, vs triamcinolone crystalline suspension (TAcs), was not significant, and testing stopped there. I found no numeric effect sizes in the sources retrieved.
- Knee Phase 3 design, per [Springer review](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40265-019-01083-3): 161 ZILRETTA vs 162 saline, 24 weeks.
- Knee Phase 2b: pain improvement vs placebo was significant at weeks 1–11 (p≤0.036) and week 13 (p=0.039), per the same review.
- A [post hoc analysis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34791634/) attributed variable knee results partly to enrollment criteria. The knee trial required moderate-to-severe ADP (≥5), while this trial requires ≥4 and ≤9.

**Other diseases and same-mechanism drugs**
- Single intra-articular steroid injections in knee OA: a [review](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2772654123000818) describes the effect vs saline as modest, lasting about 2–4 weeks.
- Recurrent steroid injections showed [no benefit over placebo](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S106345842200838X) for pain or function at 12–24 months.
- Shoulder-specific steroid evidence is thin; a [feasibility pilot](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11126843/) notes that injection data are concentrated in hip and knee. In adhesive capsulitis, a placebo-controlled trial found both steroid doses beat placebo (same pilot).

**Base rate of primary endpoint success in this disease:** Not found.

**Sponsor and investigator statements**
- A [March 2026 letter to stockholders](https://investor.pacira.com/news-releases/news-release-details/pacira-biosciences-reaffirms-commitment-shareholder-value) listed an "interim analysis" from this Phase 3 as a 2026 milestone. The registration record states no data monitoring committee, so the interim's nature is unclear. Later statements mention only topline results.
- Pacira recorded a [$25.9M in-process R&D impairment](https://nadiralpha.com/en/stocks/pcrx-pacira-biosciences-inc/) for the shoulder indication in Q3 2025, citing revised trial completion timelines (secondary aggregator; not verified against the filing).
- Viatris [agreed to acquire Pacira](https://tickeron.com/blogs/pacira-biosciences-pcrx-q3-earnings-preview-as-viatris-acquisition-nears-30115/) in October 2026, with closing expected by end of November (secondary source).
- Powering assumptions, sample-size justification, and design changes: not found in sources reviewed. The record's estimated enrollment is 150 (2:1 randomization).

**RESULT ALREADY PUBLIC:** Not found. I found no topline result. As of April 2026, the sponsor expected to finish recruiting in late Q3 2026, with topline data soon after ("complete recruitment for the study in late Q3 2026, with topline results expected soon after this milestone"; https://www.clinicaltrialsarena.com/news/realta-life-sciences-40m-financing-phase-ii-hie-pegtarazimod/).

**Earlier RLS-0071 data (no efficacy readout found)**
- Phase 1 healthy adults: 42 of 56 enrolled received drug; no clinically significant safety changes (https://www.biospace.com/realta-life-sciences-rls-0071-demonstrates-excellent-safety-profile-and-confirmed-target-engagement-in-first-in-human-phase-1-clinical-trial). The authors noted the design is not powered to achieve statistical significance for biomarkers (https://transmedcomms.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s41231-022-00134-4).
- Neonatal PK: 10 infants (8 moderate, 2 severe) at 3 mg/kg; kinetics were bi-exponential and fell within previously established safety limits (https://realtalifesciences.com/abstracts/pharmacokinetics-of-rls-0071-a-novel-anti-inflammatory-peptide-in-newborns-with-moderate-or-severe-hypoxic-ischemic-encephalopathy/). No efficacy data.
- Biomarkers: among 19 newborns, MPO in moderate HIE was 6.7 times higher than healthy adult controls (P = .003) (https://www.contemporarypediatrics.com/view/pegtarazimod-data-confirms-inflammation-biomarkers-in-hypoxic-ischemic-encephalopathy-infants).
- Rat model: the company reports anti-inflammatory effects equivalent to therapeutic hypothermia and 6% greater neuron density than hypothermia alone (https://realtalifesciences.com/news/realta-publishes-data-demonstrating-rls-0071-pegtarazimod-reduces-brain-inflammation-in-preclinical-hypoxic-ischemic-encephalopathy-model/). I found no p-values for this.

**Other diseases**
- Inhaled LPS challenge in healthy adults: sputum neutrophils fell by about half at 6 h (p=0.04), n≈30 analysed (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39286057). This is not a disease trial.
- A COVID-19 lung injury trial is registered (NCT04574869), but I found no results.

**Same mechanism in HIE:** I found no results for other complement or MPO inhibitors in HIE.

**Endpoint base rates and comparator**
- The closest precedent is HEAL, a phase 3 erythropoietin trial on top of cooling. Death or neurodevelopmental impairment was 52.5% vs 49.5% (RR 1.03; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35830641/). Its MRI injury outcome also did not reduce the overall likelihood of brain injury (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11249061/).
- Earlier small erythropoietin phase 2 data had shown less brain injury on MRI with n=50 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5980685/). Small-trial MRI signals did not hold up at scale.
- Cooling is the standard of care and the active comparator in both arms. Its benefit is real: in the NICHD trial, the primary outcome fell from 62% to 44% (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7363785/ cites the same class of trials; see also https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13616151).
- I found no published MRI-endpoint efficacy trial of a neonatal HIE adjunct that succeeded.

**Sponsor statements**
- Timing has slipped. In July 2025 the company expected to report an interim clinical data readout in the second half of 2025 (https://realtalifesciences.com/news/realta-publishes-data-demonstrating-rls-0071-pegtarazimod-reduces-brain-inflammation-in-preclinical-hypoxic-ischemic-encephalopathy-model/). I found no such readout.
- Enrollment: the 2023 plan was about 40 in Stage 1 (https://realtalifesciences.com/news/realta-doses-first-patient-in-phase-2-star-study-of-rls-0071-for-hie-in-newborns/). In April 2026 the sponsor said it would accelerate recruitment toward a target of 70 infants, which suggests slow accrual. The record lists 173.
- Endpoints: a 2023 release called safety the primary endpoint (same link as above). The April 2026 article says the primary endpoints include adverse events and MRI, while the record lists MRI only. The sponsor is also pursuing accelerated approval based on surrogate endpoints (https://www.clinicaltrialsarena.com/news/realta-life-sciences-40m-financing-phase-ii-hie-pegtarazimod/).
- Powering, interim analyses, and DSMB dose-escalation decisions: I found no public statements.

**Evidence brief: SUSTAIN (NCT06568367), solriamfetol in shift work disorder**

**Result status:** No SUSTAIN result is public. Axsome's November 2026 update still lists topline data for the second half of 2027 ([SEC Q3 2026 release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1579428/000119312526442628/axsm-ex99_1.htm)). This conflicts with the record's 2026-12 primary completion date. Earlier Axsome guidance expected topline in 2026 ([Sleep Review, 2025](https://sleepreviewmag.com/sleep-disorders/hypersomnias/narcolepsy/axsome-submit-narcolepsy-drug-candidate-axs-12-fda/)). No reason for the slip was given.

**Closest prior trial (same drug, disease, and endpoint)**
- An investigator-led, Axsome- and Jazz-funded RCT of 78 early-morning shift workers gave 4 weeks of treatment. Solriamfetol lengthened MWT sleep latency by 9.4 minutes versus placebo (95% CI 5.7–13.0; P<0.001) ([NEJM Evidence](https://evidence.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/EVIDoa2500190)).
- Limits: the population had minimal comorbidity and no pre-test polysomnography ([NeurologyLive](https://www.neurologylive.com/view/solriamfetol-significantly-reduces-excessive-sleepiness-shift-work-disorder-study-shows)). Objective workplace performance was not measured ([same source](https://www.neurologylive.com/view/solriamfetol-significantly-reduces-excessive-sleepiness-shift-work-disorder-study-shows)). The trial was not powered for SUSTAIN's 12-week design, and the effect may shrink with longer follow-up.

**Same drug, other diseases (MWT primary endpoints)**
- Narcolepsy (TONES 2): 300 mg gave a 12.3-minute MWT gain versus 2.1 minutes for placebo (all P<0.0001) ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30694576/)).
- OSA (TONES 3): both coprimary endpoints were met at all doses (P<0.05) ([PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6835071/)).
- OSA in China: a 11.77-minute MWT difference at week 12 (P<0.0001) ([NeurologyLive](https://www.neurologylive.com/view/solriamfetol-improves-wakefulness-phase-3-trial-obstructive-sleep-apnea)).
- Major depression (PARADIGM): missed the primary MADRS endpoint. Only a prespecified severe-EDS subgroup looked better, and the study was not powered for subgroups ([GlobeNewswire](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/04/01/3053170/33090/en/Axsome-Therapeutics-Announces-Topline-Results-of-PARADIGM-Phase-3-Proof-of-Concept-Trial-of-Solriamfetol-in-Major-Depressive-Disorder-MDD-with-and-without-Excessive-Daytime-Sleepin.html)).

**Same-mechanism and comparator evidence in shift work disorder**
- Modafinil, the approved comparator class, is the main reference. Its 12-week trial (n=209, night shifts) reported 74% versus 36% with at least minimal improvement ([NEJM Clinician](https://clinician.nejm.org/modafinil-shift-work-sleep-disorder-JG200508300000005)).
- A 2026 meta-analysis judged modafinil's SWSD results inconsistent across outcomes ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42468246/)). An AASM review found a 1.40-minute MSLT gain in one RCT, with low certainty ([PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13695647)).
- I found no SWD-specific placebo-response data for the MWT.

**Powering, interims, enrollment, design**
- Axsome's pipeline slide lists SUSTAIN at N=450 with topline in 2027 ([SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1579428/000095017025063158/axsm-ex99_1.htm)). The record lists 520 estimated enrollment, 49 sites, and no DMC.
- I found no statement on powering, interim analyses, enrollment difficulties, or design changes for SUSTAIN.

**Forecasting notes**
- Two co-primary endpoints: MWT and a CGI-S sleepiness rating. Success may depend on both.
- Prior solriamfetol MWT effects in narcolepsy and OSA were large, but the one SWD trial was small and short.

**Same mechanism in this disease:** Not searched/no findings.

**Endpoint hit rate and comparator:** I found no data on how often FI cell or bulking trials met a frequency-reduction endpoint versus placebo. The comparator is a vehicle placebo, and the SUI result suggests placebo response may be high in this product's trials.

**Sponsor and investigator statements**
- A Veristat (CRO) release reported onboarding 26 sites and enrolling more than 100 participants with >95% study adherence. The registry lists 200 as estimated enrollment. [Synapse organization page (Business Wire release)](https://synapse.patsnap.com/organization/f067c4cf6cee14850a1b8fedaa6d3f7b)

- Cook MyoSite is currently pursuing FDA approval for iltamiocel (July 2026 news item), but no regulatory filing for FI was found.
- A different Cook MyoSite trial (CELLEBRATE, SUI) had its target enrollment cut from 260 to 96 in 2024, per LARVOL. This is a different indication and may not be relevant. [LARVOL](https://sigma.larvol.com/product.php?e1=950581&tab=newstrac)

**Bottom line for the forecaster:** Open-label FI data are encouraging but uncontrolled. The sponsor's only randomized analogue in SUI missed its primary endpoint against a high placebo response. No public DigniFI result or enrollment-trouble statement was found.

- Other diseases: I found no efficacy data for 225Ac-DOTATATE outside GEP-NETs. RYZ101 is in early HR+ breast cancer trials, with no results found.

**Same-mechanism and benchmark trials**
- NETTER-1 (177Lu-DOTATATE, midgut, post-SSA, ~231 patients): median PFS was not reached in the 177Lu-DOTATATE arm compared to 8.4 months in the high-dose octreotide arm (hazard ratio 0.21). Source: pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7227421/. The control there is a weak comparator.
- NETTER-2 (first-line, grade 2–3): median PFS was 22·8 months in the 177Lu-Dotatate group vs 8·5 months (stratified hazard ratio 0·276). Source: pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38851203. Different population.
- COMPETE (177Lu-edotreotide vs everolimus, grade 1–2, n=309, 2:1): median PFS 23·9 vs 14·1 months (stratified hazard ratio 0·67; p=0·022). Source: thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)00604-5/abstract. Central ORR was 21.9% vs 4.2% for everolimus (oncozine.com, ESMO 2025 summary). Everolimus is a moderately active comparator, and the PFS effect was smaller than in NETTER-1/2. 53 everolimus patients (52%) later received PRRT, which confounds OS.
- Control arm here is mixed: high-dose or high-frequency somatostatin analogues, everolimus, or sunitinib (per the BMS release). Heterogeneous control arms make the effect hard to interpret.

**Endpoint base rate:** I did not find a systematic count. Among the three randomized radioligand trials above, all met PFS.

**Sponsor statements on design, powering, and delays**
- The readout came from a planned interim analysis. The registry's 143-event target is the only sizing detail I found.
- I found no statements on enrollment problems, design changes, or delays. Enrollment is complete and the registry lists the trial as active, not recruiting.
- Enrolled patients continue on protocol for overall survival follow-up (followed for overall survival, OncLive).

**Forecasting note:** The topline announcement already reports a positive primary PFS result. Any forecast should check whether it concerns the interim analysis already reported or a later final analysis.

**Evidence brief: NCT07499674 (abenacianine, VISUALIZE 2)**

**Result status:** No result for this trial is public. Its registry shows no posted results, and the sponsor says the NDA is planned for 2027 ([Vergent, Jul 2026](https://www.vergentbio.com/press-releases/vergent-bioscience-announces-publication-in-the-annals-of-surgical-oncology-demonstrating-abenacianine-with-intraoperative-molecular-imaging-improved-tumor-visualization-during-lung-cancer-surgery)).

**Earlier trials, same drug and disease**
- Phase 2b VISUALIZE (NCT06145048, n=89, single-arm): 40 of 89 (44.9%, 95% CI 34.4–55.9%) had ≥1 CSE. The lower bound excluded a ≤10% null (P<.0001). In vivo NIR sensitivity was 0.841 and PPV 0.750 ([Targeted Oncology](https://www.targetedonc.com/view/abenacianine-identifies-occult-lung-tumors-improves-surgical-margins)).
- CSE breakdown: 33 were localization of a preoperatively identified lesion, 3 occult lesions, 8 margins, 1 lymph node (same source). Under this trial's registry wording, only the localization and occult categories clearly count, which gives about 36/89 (~40%). This is my calculation.
- Dose-ranging phase 2 (n=27, Australia): 0.05 mg/kg showed no lesions. 0.16 mg/kg dosed 12–36 h pre-surgery identified 3 of 4 lesions. Timing was tested only out to 36 h ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40985702/)). The phase 3 window extends to 96 h, which is untested.
- The sponsor's earlier press releases say the phase 2b trial met its primary endpoint ([Vergent](https://www.vergentbio.com/news-2025-may22)).

**Other diseases and same-mechanism agents**
- Abenacianine is a cathepsin-activated probe. Cathepsins are overexpressed across many solid tumors ([Vergent](https://www.vergentbio.com/press-releases/vergent-bioscience-initiates-phase-3-visualize-2-pivotal-study-of-abenacianine-(vgt-309)-for-tumor-visualization-during-lung-cancer-surgery)). Preclinical work covers breast, colorectal and skin models ([Stanford/Kennedy](https://med.stanford.edu/content/dam/sm/bogyolab/documents/KennedyClinCancerRes2023.pdf)). I found no human results outside lung.
- No other cathepsin-probe trial results in lung were found.

**Comparator and base rate**
- The closest precedent is the pafolacianine (folate-receptor) phase 3 ELUCIDATE trial. It randomized 112 patients 10:1 and reached a 53% CSE rate against a prespecified 10% limit (P<.0001). No drug-related serious adverse events were reported ([ScienceDirect](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S002252232300185X)).
- Pafolacianine's real-world false-negative rate was about 37.5% for deep lesions (>20 mm), versus 75% for the surgeon ([Clin Lung Cancer](https://www.clinical-lung-cancer.com/article/S1525-7304(24)00247-X/fulltext)).
- The control here is standard surgery with white light, palpation, and preoperative imaging. Investigators describe the control as robust usual care, with the agent given to all patients ([Targeted Oncology](https://www.targetedonc.com/view/abenacianine-identifies-occult-lung-tumors-improves-surgical-margins)).

**Sponsor and investigator statements**
- The sponsor reports enrollment is "advancing rapidly" and has added infusion-timing flexibility out to four days ([Vergent, Jul 2026](https://www.vergentbio.com/press-releases/vergent-bioscience-announces-publication-in-the-annals-of-surgical-oncology-demonstrating-abenacianine-with-intraoperative-molecular-imaging-improved-tumor-visualization-during-lung-cancer-surgery)).
- The company's press release says 10 sites, while the registry lists 9 ([Vergent](https://www.vergentbio.com/press-releases/vergent-bioscience-initiates-phase-3-visualize-2-pivotal-study-of-abenacianine-(vgt-309)-for-tumor-visualization-during-lung-cancer-surgery)).
- No statements on interim analyses, a formal power calculation, or design changes were found. The registry has no DMC.
- Registry primary completion is 2026-12, which is very close to today's date. This is likely too early, so a date slip is plausible. I found no reported delay.

**Forecasting notes**
- The endpoint is a single-arm-derived rate tested against a fixed 10% null. Phase 2b's 45% point estimate clears that comfortably.
- The gap is the relative comparison. The randomized "NIR vs. no NIR" design in 12 control patients is small.
- No peer-reviewed phase 3 data exist yet.

Keymed's 2026 H1 report says the adolescent SAR Phase III started in July 2026 and gives no readout ([Keymed H1 2026](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/keymed-biosciences-announces-2026-h1-results-and-business-updates-302856519.html)).

**Prior stapokibart SAR trials (adults)**
- **Phase 3 PHECDA** (n=108, eosinophils ≥300, placebo add-on to standard care): the 2-week rTNSS difference was −1.3 (95% CI −2.0 to −0.6; P=0.0008) and the 4-week difference was −1.7 (P=0.0002) ([Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-025-03651-5)). Secondary endpoints were significantly improved and adverse events were comparable to placebo (same source).
- **Phase 2 MERAK** (investigator-initiated) missed the same primary endpoint in the full population: every-two-weeks dosing gave −1.0 (97.5% CI −2.3 to 0.2; P=0.065), and weekly dosing gave P=0.67. The eosinophil ≥300 subgroup, about 47% of patients, reached −1.9 (P=0.0095) ([Expert review, Taylor & Francis](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/1750743X.2025.2554562)). Read this as subgroup-driven evidence. The adult phase 3 was built on that subgroup, and this adolescent trial inherits the design.

**Adolescent data**
- Only a 20-child retrospective case series, with no control group and a VAS endpoint, is published ([Frontiers in Allergy](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/allergy/articles/10.3389/falgy.2026.1785270/full)). The authors call for randomized trials.
- A separate single-arm adolescent safety/PK study, NCT07617324, is registered with about 15 participants ([ClinicalTrials.gov](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07617324)). It is not this trial.

**Other diseases**
- Stapokibart's adult atopic dermatitis and nasal polyp programs are positive in phase 3, and it is approved in China for SAR ([Drugs & Therapy Perspectives](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40267-026-01256-7)). This shows the drug works in type 2 disease. It does not establish seasonal nasal endpoints in adolescents.

**Same mechanism (dupilumab, IL-4Rα)**
- In a grass-pollen nasal-challenge phase 2a (adults, n=103), dupilumab added to immunotherapy did not significantly improve the primary endpoint over immunotherapy alone. Dupilumab alone also failed to reduce it significantly ([Corren et al., JACI 2021](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34429614/)). This is a challenge model, not natural-season symptoms.
- I found no natural-season dupilumab phase 3 in SAR.

**Base rates and comparator**
- I found no systematic success rate for TNSS-primary SAR trials. The FDA guidance treats rTNSS as the standard primary endpoint for SAR drugs ([FDA guidance](https://www.fda.gov/files/drugs/published/Allergic-Rhinitis--Developing-Drug-Products-for-Treatment-Guidance-for-Industry.pdf)).
- The comparator is placebo added to background care, not an active drug. I found no evidence that background therapy is unusually hard to beat.

**Sponsor statements and operational risk**
- I found no sponsor statement on powering, interim analyses, or design changes for this trial.
- Timing is tight (my inference): the record shows a start on 2026-08-13 and primary completion in 2026-12 for 136 estimated participants. Enrollment has to happen during the pollen season. The pediatric case series treated patients in spring and in August–October ([Frontiers](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/allergy/articles/10.3389/falgy.2026.1785270/full)). Enrollment shortfall is a plausible risk.

**Safety signal to note**
- In the adult SAR trial, treatment-induced anti-drug antibodies occurred in 6% after the double-blind and follow-up periods ([Expert review](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/1750743X.2025.2554562)).

**1. Earlier trials of this drug in this disease**
I found no trial of empagliflozin added to metformin plus alogliptin. The closest precedents are Korean empagliflozin add-on trials that used the same 24-week HbA1c primary endpoint:
- Empagliflozin 10 mg and 25 mg added to metformin plus sitagliptin (n=172) lowered HbA1c versus placebo by 0.7% and 0.8%, both p<0.0001. Participants were randomised 1:1:1 to empagliflozin 10 mg, empagliflozin 25 mg, or placebo. ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41417560/))
- Empagliflozin added to metformin plus linagliptin (Diabetes Care, 2017) gave differences of −0.79% and −0.70% versus placebo, both P<0.001. ([Diabetes Care](https://care.diabetesjournals.org/content/40/2/201))
- The original EMPA-REG MET trial (metformin alone, 24 weeks) reported −0.70% and −0.77% versus a placebo change of −0.13%. ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24722494/?dopt=Abstract))

**2. Same drug in other diseases; same mechanism in this disease**
I did not search other indications; they add little to an HbA1c endpoint in T2DM. For the same add-on logic, a DPP-4 inhibitor was added to metformin plus empagliflozin in Korea:
- Anagliptin 100 mg BID with empagliflozin 25 mg (n=197 analysed): −0.80% versus placebo, p<0.0001. At week 24, the least-squares mean HbA1c change was -0.83 % with anagliptin versus -0.03 % with placebo. ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42036072/))
- Anagliptin with empagliflozin 10 mg (n=195): −0.57%, p<0.0001. ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43036268))
- A sitagliptin/empagliflozin fixed-dose combination on metformin plus sitagliptin (n=230) showed −0.54% and −0.61% versus placebo, both p<0.0001. ([Wiley](https://dom-pubs.pericles-prod.literatumonline.com/doi/10.1111/dom.70669))
- I found no published alogliptin add-on trial with an SGLT2 inhibitor.

**3. Base rate and comparator**
In the small set of trials above, every HbA1c primary endpoint was met versus placebo. This is not a systematic count. The comparator is weak: placebo arms fell by about 0.03% to 0.2% over 24 weeks. In the anagliptin trial, the least-squares mean HbA1c change was -0.03 % with placebo. The record calls the control arm a placebo comparator, but the arm description lists only metformin and alogliptin, so the forecaster should check whether an empagliflozin-matched placebo was used.

**4. Sponsor or investigator statements**
I found nothing on powering, interim analyses, enrollment trouble, design changes, or delays. The record reports no data monitoring committee, an estimated enrollment of 171 at one South Korean site, and a planned primary completion of 2026-12, with the last update in August 2025. The 171 target is similar to the Korean precedents, which had about 170 to 200 patients. Nothing I found suggests a design change.

Formal statistical testing is not provided, as this proof-of-concept study was closed prior to reaching the study's prespecified sample size ([Biohaven PR, May 2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1935979/000193597926000048/exhibit991may26thpressrele.htm)). Median time to a second GTC seizure was 141 days on drug vs 47 on placebo ([same](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1935979/000193597926000048/exhibit991may26thpressrele.htm)). Focal data are open-label only: 54% of participants on opakalim 75 mg once daily achieved a ≥50% reduction in seizure frequency over any consecutive six months (n>100) ([Biohaven PR, June 2026](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/biohaven-completes-enrollment-in-rise-3-pivotal-focal-epilepsy-study-with-opakalim-a-selective-kv7-27-3-activator-302813944.html)). Uncontrolled, so not comparable to placebo.

([StockTitan](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/BHVN/biohaven-reports-new-clinical-data-in-epilepsy-with-opakalim-a-nmpji5zs7ptz.html)). In bipolar mania, BHV-7000 did not statistically differentiate from the comparator arm on the primary efficacy endpoint ([Biohaven FY2024 results](https://ir.biohaven.com/news-releases/news-release-details/biohaven-reports-recent-business-developments-and-fourth-quarter)).

**Same mechanism in this disease:** Azetukalner (Kv7.2/7.3 opener) is the closest comparator. In Phase 3 X-TOLE2 (n=374, 12 weeks), median monthly focal seizure change was -53.2% at 25 mg, -34.5% at 15 mg, and -10.4% with placebo ([Xenon](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/03/09/3251686/33485/en/Xenon-Announces-Positive-Topline-Data-from-Phase-3-X-TOLE2-Study-of-Azetukalner-in-Focal-Onset-Seizures-FOS.html)). Its Phase 2b predecessor showed median seizure-frequency reductions of 52.8% at 25 mg versus 18.2% with placebo ([NeurologyLive](https://www.neurologylive.com/view/full-x-tole2-data-detail-azetukalner-dose-dependent-profile-focal-epilepsy)). Dizziness was 20.5% of patients receiving azetukalner compared with 3.2% in the placebo group ([NeurologyLive](https://www.neurologylive.com/view/phase-3-x-tole2-data-support-nda-submission-azetukalner-focal-onset-seizures)).

**Base rate and comparator:** I found no compiled success rate for this endpoint. Qualitatively, all five third-generation ASMs have demonstrated significant efficacy vs. placebo ([Narrative review](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13615192)). That is a selected, published set, so it overstates success rates. Placebo arms in these trials vary; X-TOLE2's was low, with a ~12.75 seizures/month baseline ([NeurologyLive](https://www.neurologylive.com/view/full-x-tole2-data-detail-azetukalner-dose-dependent-profile-focal-epilepsy)).

**Sponsor statements, powering, and operations:**
- The FDA issued a partial clinical hold on 2026-09-04 over insufficient information related to a specific metabolite found in rodent testing. New enrollment is paused ([8-K](https://ir.biohaven.com/static-files/c4ca575c-17c6-4c8e-8dd4-d92dfc560f72)).
- Enrollment in the trial was already complete and randomized before the hold ([AllSci](https://allsci.com/news/regulatory/fda-clinical-hold-opakalim-partial-on-biohavens/)). The sponsor says the hold does not affect its timeline.
- The IGE study closed early partly for enrollment challenges and strategic portfolio prioritization. That is an enrollment-trouble signal for this program.
- I found no public statements on interim analyses, powering, or design changes for this trial.

**Evidence brief: NCT05884255 (177Lu-oxodotreotide + standard LAR octreotide vs high-dose LAR octreotide, pancreatic NETs)**

**1. Earlier trials of this drug in this disease**
- No randomized trial of this drug in pancreatic NETs appears in my search. A CADTH review says the efficacy or safety of lutetium (177Lu) oxodotreotide in patients with pNETs has not been evaluated in randomized clinical trials ([source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK602624/)).
- The closest Chinese analogue, XT-XTR008-3-01 (grade 1–2, later-line, all GEP-NET origins, 59% pancreatic), is a [Annals of Oncology report](https://www.annalsofoncology.org/article/S0923-7534(25)04697-6/fulltext). It enrolled 196 patients and had 78 PFS events, median PFS was not reached versus 5.8 months; stratified hazard ratio (HR) 0.06 (P < 0.0001). The OS trend was HR 0.24, P = 0.0550, with immature data. This was monotherapy without SSA, which differs from the trial under review.
- The commentary on that trial notes its very short follow-up (11 months) and suggests the striking PFS HR of 0.06 derives from the poorer than expected results of the control arm ([source](https://www.annalsofoncology.org/article/S0923-7534(25)04786-6/fulltext)).
- NETTER-1 (midgut, second-line, 231 patients, same comparator design as this trial) reported a HR of 0.18 (95% CI: 0.11, 0.29; p < 0.0001) for PFS ([source](https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/JCO.2021.39.15_suppl.4112)). The final OS result was median OS 48.0 months vs 36.3 months; HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.60–1.17), p = 0.30. Control-arm crossover was high (41/114 (36%)).

**2. Other diseases and other drugs in this disease**
- NETTER-2 (first-line, grade 2–3) reported a pancreatic-NET PFS HR of 0.336 (95% CI, 0.200–0.562) ([source](https://www.cancernetwork.com/view/177lu-dotatate-combo-shows-consistent-efficacy-across-gep-net-subgroups)).
- In the OCLURANDOM study, 177Lu-octreotate had an 80.5% PFS at 12 months versus 42% with sunitinib ([source](https://acsjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/cncr.35463)).
- I did not search other indications for this drug.

**3. Endpoint base rate and comparator strength**
- The control arm is weak. Median PFS with high-dose octreotide was 5.8 months in XT-XTR008 and 8.5 months in NETTER-1 (see above). A meta-analysis reports median PFS was 30.87 months (95% CI, 22.71-39.04) for 177Lu-DOTATATE across single-arm and other studies. That is not a comparative estimate.
- I found no systematic tally of how often PFS primary endpoints were met in GEP-NET phase 3 trials.

**4. Sponsor or investigator statements**
- I found no HengRui statements on powering, interim analyses, enrollment, design changes, or delays. AdisInsight lists the program only as being developed by Jiangsu HengRui Medicine for the treatment of gastrointestinal pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours ([source](https://adisinsight.springer.com/drugs/800073974)).

**5. Whether the trial's result is public**
- I found no announced result for this trial or any HengRui press release on it.

**Forecasting notes**
- The PFS endpoint is assessed by BICR with follow-up of up to one year. The strongest comparable effect, from XT-XTR008, was based on short follow-up and a weak control arm. Both points favor a large effect size, but the single-sponsor, open-label design and the one-year horizon limit the comparison.

**RESULT ALREADY PUBLIC: No.** I found no results announcement for NCT05780567. I also found no sponsor or investigator statements on its interim analyses, powering, enrollment, or delays. The only recent sponsor mention says the adjuvant study is currently underway ([Sino Biopharm, 2026](https://www.en.sbpgroup.com/userfiles/files/E26044841-Sino%20Bio-PA.pdf)).

**Prior TQB3616 (culmerciclib) efficacy: advanced disease only**
- Previously treated patients (CULMINATE, n=293, with fulvestrant): at a prespecified interim analysis, investigator-assessed median PFS was 16.6 months versus 7.5 months with placebo ([Signal Transduct Target Ther, 2025](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41392-025-02475-6)). Response rate was 40.2% versus 12.1% ([same source via ResearchGate](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/380080864_Discovery_and_preclinical_evaluations_of_TQB3616_a_novel_CDK4-biased_inhibitor)).
- First-line (CULMINATE-2, n=432): PFS hazard ratio 0.56 (95% CI 0.40–0.78), median not reached versus 20.2 months ([HMP Global Learning Network](https://www.hmpgloballearningnetwork.com/site/onc/news/culmerciclib-plus-fulvestrant-patients-hr-positive-her2-negative-advanced-breast)).
- China approved the drug for previously treated advanced disease in December 2025 ([ResearchGate summary](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/380080864_Discovery_and_preclinical_evaluations_of_TQB3616_a_novel_CDK4-biased_inhibitor)).
- No early-stage or adjuvant efficacy data found.
- Other diseases: not searched beyond preclinical work. In side-by-side preclinical assays, the compound outperformed palbociclib and abemaciclib on enzymatic and cellular potency ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38670537/)).

**Same mechanism, adjuvant HR+/HER2− setting**
- monarchE (abemaciclib): at 5 years, invasive disease-free survival was 86.7% versus 80.6% with endocrine therapy alone (HR 0.68) ([review, Breast Cancer journal](https://www.mdpi.com/2227-9059/14/4/893)).
- NATALEE (ribociclib): at 6 years, iDFS was 83.2% versus 77.9%. Overall survival HR was 0.809 at the prespecified 6-year analysis, a nominal result ([CancerNetwork, ESMO 2026](https://www.cancernetwork.com/view/adjuvant-ribociclib-improves-os-at-6-years-in-hr-her2--early-breast-cancer)).
- Pooled monarchE and NATALEE: invasive recurrence HR 0.69 ([PubMed meta-analysis, 2026](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42593362/)).
- Palbociclib (PALLAS, PENELOPE-B) did not improve iDFS or OS in the same review ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42593362/)).
- An earlier pooled analysis of three trials found iDFS HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.71–1.01), not significant ([PMC, 2021](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8010395/)).

**Comparator and endpoint context**
- Endocrine therapy alone is the comparator, and the control arm here receives the same endocrine therapy. The endpoint matches the adjuvant trials above.
- Critics argue the open-label adjuvant trials may overstate iDFS through informative censoring, and call for placebo-controlled trials ([ScienceDirect, 2024](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0959804924008487)). This trial's double-blind design addresses that concern.
- Benefit per patient is modest. One commentary calls the absolute recurrence reductions modest and notes the toxicity burden ([Annals of Oncology, 2025](https://www.annalsofoncology.org/article/S0923-7534(25)04956-7/fulltext)).

**Base rate:** Of four adjuvant CDK4/6 phase 3 trials, two (monarchE, NATALEE) met iDFS, and two (PALLAS, PENELOPE-B) did not ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42593362/)). Only a small share of the CDK4/6 adjuvant evidence comes from a double-blind design.

**Bottom line:** No readout, powering statements, or design changes are public. The record's primary completion date (2026-12) and its active-not-recruiting status suggest a readout may come soon. Evidence for the mechanism in early disease is mixed, and no early-stage TQB3616 data exist.

**RESULT ALREADY PUBLIC:** This trial (APOLLO, NCT04344158) has reported. At the second interim OS analysis (data cutoff 29 Jan 2024), median OS was 16.5 vs 13.2 months with anlotinib plus penpulimab vs sorafenib, HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.55–0.87), p=0.0014 ([Lancet Oncology 2025](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lanonc/article/PIIS1470-2045(25)00190-1/abstract); [ESMO 2024 abstract, Annals of Oncology](https://www.annalsofoncology.org/article/S0923-7534(24)03860-2/fulltext)). The record's "active, not recruiting" status is out of date.

**Discrepancy:** The record lists OS as the sole primary outcome. Publications describe dual primary endpoints, PFS by independent review and OS ([Annals](https://www.annalsofoncology.org/article/S0923-7534(24)03860-2/fulltext)).

**1. Earlier trials of this regimen**
- Phase Ib/II AK105-203 (single-arm, ORR primary): ORR 31% and DCR 82.8% ([Frontiers](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/oncology/articles/10.3389/fonc.2021.684867/xml)).
- Phase 3 APOLLO PFS: 6.9 vs 2.8 months, HR 0.52 (p<0.0001) ([Lancet Oncology](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lanonc/article/PIIS1470-2045(25)00190-1/abstract)).
- Anlotinib monotherapy, phase II ALTER-0802: primary endpoint was 12-week PFS rate, 80.8% in the first-line cohort (n=26) ([Hepatology International](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12072-021-10171-0)).
- Retrospective anlotinib vs sorafenib (n=158, second line): OS 13.0 vs 11.0 months (P=0.010); PFS and ORR not different ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40783436/)).

**2. Other diseases and same-mechanism drugs**
- Several ICI–TKI combinations (COSMIC-312, LEAP-002) failed to show OS gains over sorafenib; CARES-310 (camrelizumab plus rivoceranib) succeeded ([JGO](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12972027/)).
- Penpulimab plus anlotinib in NSCLC gave an ORR of 57.1% in a small study ([Lancet Respir Med/AK105-302 context](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S2213260023004319)). I found no other-disease OS data.

**3. Endpoint base rate and comparator**
- Sorafenib is a weak comparator. In SHARP, OS was 10.7 vs 7.9 months with placebo ([NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa0708857)). Asian median OS on sorafenib was 6.5–8.9 months ([PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12335444/)).
- Critics note sorafenib no longer reflects standard care. Contemporary first-line OS was 19.2 months with atezolizumab–bevacizumab and 23.7 months with nivolumab–ipilimumab ([JGO](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12972027/)).
- I found no pooled base rate of primary-endpoint success for HCC phase 3 trials.

**4. Sponsor and investigator statements**
- The planned OS interim was set at 332 deaths; 338 occurred ([Annals](https://www.annalsofoncology.org/article/S0923-7534(24)03860-2/fulltext)).
- Enrollment ran from August 2020 to June 2023, with 649 randomized ([Lancet Oncology](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lanonc/article/PIIS1470-2045(25)00190-1/abstract)).
- Investigators said the findings "require verification in other regions" ([ASCO Post](https://ascopost.com/news/may-2025/anlotinib-plus-penpulimab-in-first-line-treatment-of-unresectable-hepatocellular-carcinoma/)).
- Caveats: the trial was open-label with no placebo ([JGO](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12972027/)). Subsequent PD-1 use was higher in the sorafenib arm (21% vs 13%), which may dilute the OS gap ([JGO](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12972027/)).
- Regulatory: China's NMPA accepted a supplemental application in November 2024 ([BioSpace/Akeso](https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/akesos-penpulimab-combination-therapy-for-first-line-treatment-of-hepatocellular-carcinoma-accepted-by-nmpa)).
- Powering assumptions, design changes, and delays: not found.

**Result status:** No QL2107 Phase 3 result was found. A Cipla partnership release from September 2026 says no clinical data has been disclosed publicly to date ([BioPharm International](https://www.biopharminternational.com/view/cipla-partners-with-qilu-pharmaceutical-to-commercialize-a-keytruda-biosimilar-in-the-us)).

**Earlier QL2107 data**
- The only QL2107 study found is a pharmacokinetic trial in resected (adjuvant) NSCLC, with the primary purpose to demonstrate pharmacokinetic similarity ([Synapse](https://synapse.patsnap.com/drug/13f20d3c35b34c08921e208b0e8d6a86)). No efficacy results or effect sizes were found.

**Closest analogue: Samsung Bioepis SB27 (same design)**
- Phase 3 in metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC: 555 patients across 14 countries ([TechTimes](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/330213/20261106/samsung-bioepis-puts-keytruda-biosimilar-fda-review-full-phase-3-lung-cancer-trial-data.htm)). Both arms received 200 mg IV every three weeks with pemetrexed; carboplatin on the same schedule for the first four cycles ([Korea Biomedical Review](https://www.koreabiomed.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=33773)).
- Week-24 ORR was 34.6 percent versus 37.9 percent with Keytruda (my calculation: ratio ≈0.91). The 90% CI for the ORR ratio was 0.737-1.071, within the prespecified margin of 0.712-1.405 ([OncLive](https://www.onclive.com/view/pembrolizumab-biosimilar-meets-primary-phase-1-and-phase-3-end-points-in-nsclc)).
- The full dataset was reported later, with secondary endpoints showing high comparability ([TechTimes](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/330213/20261106/samsung-bioepis-puts-keytruda-biosimilar-fda-review-full-phase-3-lung-cancer-trial-data.htm)).

**Other pembrolizumab biosimilars**
- Formycon's FYB206 Phase 3 in NSCLC was stopped: the Phase 3 study is no longer necessary per FDA dialogue ([Pearce IP](https://www.pearceip.law/2025/02/17/formycon-to-terminate-ph-3-trial-and-pursue-us-approval-of-pembrolizumab-biosimilar-based-on-ph-1-analytical-data/)). Its pivotal Dahlia study was a PK trial in melanoma ([Targeted Oncology](https://www.targetedonc.com/view/fda-accepts-bla-pembrolizumab-biosimilar-fyb206)). Some secondary reports describe it as "positive results" ([Pearce IP](https://www.pearceip.law/2026/05/11/update-on-pembrolizumab-biosimilar-clinical-trials-2/)), which overstates the evidence for efficacy.
- Bio-Thera ended its Phase 1/3 study on similar regulatory grounds ([Pearce IP](https://www.pearceip.law/2026/05/11/update-on-pembrolizumab-biosimilar-clinical-trials-2/)).

**Comparator strength**
- In KEYNOTE-189, the reference regimen (pembrolizumab + pemetrexed-platinum) reached ORR of 47.6% versus 18.9% for placebo-chemo ([Annals of Oncology](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0923753421011467)). This is a historical trial, not a same-trial control, so it only shows the comparator is active, not that it is hard to beat in this design.

**Powering, interims, delays**
- No sponsor statements on powering, interim analyses, or enrollment problems were found.
- A Pearce IP update lists the trial as recruiting with an estimated primary completion date of December 2026 ([Pearce IP](https://www.pearceip.law/2026/05/11/update-on-pembrolizumab-biosimilar-clinical-trials-2/)). The BioPharm piece treats completion of phase 3 enrollment as the next milestone, suggesting enrollment was still open in September 2026.

**Not covered**
- Efficacy of other PD-1 agents in this setting, and results of other pembrolizumab biosimilars' efficacy trials beyond SB27, were not searched in depth.
- Pembrolizumab's efficacy in other diseases: it has accumulated approvals across more than 30 indications ([OncLive](https://www.onclive.com/view/pembrolizumab-biosimilar-meets-primary-phase-1-and-phase-3-end-points-in-nsclc)). I did not extract per-indication effect sizes.

I found no sponsor statements on powering, interim timing, enrollment problems, or design changes for this trial.

**Earlier trials of ivonescimab in TNBC**
- The only prior TNBC data are a single-arm, open-label phase 2 (NCT05227664, 35 evaluable). It reported ORR 80.0% and median PFS 9.36 months, but its primary endpoints were safety and investigator-assessed ORR, not PFS, and it had no comparator. The primary endpoints were safety and the investigator-assessed objective response rate per RECIST v.1.1. (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42587052/; https://cancernetwork.com/view/ivonescimab-chemo-combo-yields-positive-efficacy-and-safety-results-in-tnbc)
- In the PD-L1 CPS <10 subgroup, the ESMO 2024 update reported ORR 69.6% and median PFS 9.3 months (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/akesos-ivonescimab-plus-chemo-in-first-line-triple-negative-breast-cancer-showed-promising-preliminary-efficacy-and-good-safety-at-esmo-2024-302248727.html). **Same drug in other diseases**
- HARMONi (EGFR-mutant NSCLC, placebo-controlled): PFS HR 0.52 (p<0.0001), but OS HR 0.79 (p=0.057) did not reach significance. FDA issued a complete response letter on Nov 15, 2026 (https://www.onclive.com/view/dr-leighl-on-harmoni-survival-data-and-the-fda-s-decision-on-ivonescimab-in-previously-treated-egfr-mutated-nsclc; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1599298/000159929826000092/ivonescimabcrlscenariopr.htm). - HARMONi-2 (PD-L1+ NSCLC vs pembrolizumab): interim OS HR 0.73, p=0.009 (https://www.akesobio.com/en/media/akeso-news/260903/).
- HARMONi-GI1 (biliary tract, vs durvalumab plus chemo): met OS primary endpoint at a prespecified IDMC interim (https://www.akesobio.com/en/media/akeso-news/260826/).

**Comparator and PD-L1 history**
- Nab-paclitaxel plus placebo is the control. In IMpassion130, atezolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel improved ITT PFS (7.2 vs 5.5 months, HR 0.80, P=0.002), and the PD-L1-positive subgroup had HR 0.62 (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1809615). ITT OS was not significant (HR 0.84, P=0.08).
- Benefit has been confined to PD-L1-selected groups. An ASCO review notes that no immunotherapy trial has shown benefit in PD-L1-negative metastatic TNBC, and that IMpassion131 was negative (https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/EDBK-26-520506).
- KEYNOTE-355 was positive only in CPS ≥10 (median PFS 9.7 vs 5.6 months); CPS ≥1 was not significant (https://www.onclive.com/view/frontline-pembrolizumab-chemo-represents-new-standard-in-metastatic-tnbc-with-pd-l1-cps-10; https://www.theoncologynurse.com/issue-archive/2022/february-2022-vol-15-no-1/keynote-355-pembrolizumab-plus-chemotherapy-extends-survival-in-patients-with-triple-negative-breast-cancer-and-pd-l1-combined-positive-score-10).
- The ASCO review describes this trial's population as PD-L1-negative metastatic TNBC (https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/EDBK-26-520506). The registry record has no PD-L1 restriction, so the forecaster should check the enrolled PD-L1 mix. This is the main risk to a positive PFS result.

**Interim-analysis signal from the sponsor's portfolio:** In Summit's HARMONi-3 (a different, NSCLC trial), an interim PFS look showed no early efficacy signal. Summit said the interim had minimal alpha spending (https://allsci.com/news/clinical-trials/summits-ivonescimab-heads-toward-november-fda-decision-as-harmoni-3-interim-pfs-misses-threshold/). This is indirect evidence on how interim boundaries may be set.
