**Sponsor statements on powering, interims, enrollment, and delays**

- Enrollment in ECLIPSE 2 is complete, and so is the full ECLIPSE program ([Vir, Sept 2026](https://synapse.patsnap.com/drug/9a1bdae0109c4155bbe3da67fe58a1ed)).
- ECLIPSE 2 enrolls only where bulevirtide is approved ([Vir, Jul 2025](https://investors.vir.bio/news/news-details/2025/Vir-Biotechnology-Initiates-Second-Pivotal-Trial-in-Its-Global-ECLIPSE-Registrational-Program-for-Chronic-Hepatitis-Delta/default.aspx)).
- The sponsor plans a U.S. FDA submission in mid-2027 ([BioSpace](https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/vir-biotechnology-announces-primary-endpoint-met-in-pivotal-phase-3-eclipse-1-trial-for-elebsiran-and-tobevibart-in-chronic-hepatitis-delta)).
- The record's primary completion (2026-12) predates the Q1 2027 topline guidance.
- I found no statements about interim analyses, powering assumptions, or design changes for ECLIPSE 2.

**RESULT ALREADY PUBLIC:** The primary PFS endpoint was met at a prespecified interim analysis. Hengrui announced on May 18, 2026 that BICR-assessed PFS reached statistical significance; 期中分析主要终点达到统计学显著性 ([Xueqiu post on the announcement](https://xueqiu.com/1013597948/390011806)). The full data were presented at ESMO 2026 (LBA72) and published in The Lancet on October 26, 2026. Median BICR PFS was 8.3 vs 5.4 months, hazard ratio = 0.47; one-sided P < .0001 ([ASCO Post](https://ascopost.com/news/november-2026/heron-lung01-her3-directed-adc-prolongs-pfs-in-egfr-mutated-advanced-nsclc/)). The 95% CI was 0·36–0·60 ([ScienceDirect/Lancet](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0140673626018994)). Enrollment was 250 vs 248 between November 29, 2024, and January 29, 2026 ([OncoDaily](https://oncodaily.com/oncolibrary/lung-oncology/heron-lung01)). Median follow-up at the interim was 7.7 months.

**Earlier trials of this drug (same disease)**
- Phase 1 (NCT05114759), 9.0 mg/kg cohort, EGFR-mutant NSCLC: ORR 46.9% (23/49), median PFS 9.6 months; all-dose median PFS 6.7 months; ILD 8.7% ([Zhihu summary of ESMO 2024](https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/24180150968)). Single-arm, not comparable to the randomized endpoint.
- No other randomized data found.

**Other diseases:** No data found.

**Same mechanism, same disease:** HER3-DXd (HERTHENA-Lung02) met PFS, with a median progression-free survival was 5.8 months with patritumab deruxtecan versus 5.4 months with chemotherapy ([CURE](https://www.curetoday.com/view/patritumab-deruxtecan-does-not-improve-survival-outcomes-vs-chemo-in-egfr-nsclc)). OS did not improve: HR, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.79-1.22. Merck previously withdrew its biologics license application ([OncLive](https://www.onclive.com/view/patritumab-deruxtecan-does-not-improve-overall-survival-in-egfr-mutated-nsclc)). The same-setting, different-mechanism EGFR×HER3 bispecific ADC iza-bren reported 11.14 vs 5.65 months; hazard ratio (HR) 0.40 in PANKU-Lung01 ([ESMO 2026 highlights](https://webcast.cipla.com/quick-reads/conferencehighlights/esmo-2026-key-highlights-from-day-4)).

**Comparator and endpoint base rate:** The chemotherapy arm's 5.4-month median PFS in both HER3 trials suggests a modest comparator. I did not find a historical PFS hit-rate analysis for this setting.

**Sponsor and investigator statements**
- Interim analysis was prespecified; the trial is recruitment-complete and ongoing ([Lancet abstract](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01899-4/abstract)).
- No enrollment trouble, design change, or delay reported in sources found.
- Grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs were 41% vs 39% ([ASCO Post](https://ascopost.com/news/november-2026/heron-lung01-her3-directed-adc-prolongs-pfs-in-egfr-mutated-advanced-nsclc/)).
- I found no reported OS result; OS is secondary.

**Bottom line:** The record's primary endpoint has already been reported as met. The open questions are OS, which is not reported, and the durability of the PFS effect given the short follow-up.

**RESULT ALREADY PUBLIC: No.** I found no announced topline result. Enrollment finished in October 2024 ([Madrigal](https://ir.madrigalpharma.com/news-releases/news-release-details/madrigal-pharmaceuticals-completes-enrollment-clinical-outcomes)). The company's current readout guidance is late 2027 ([Q3 2026 call](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/11/03/madrigal-mdgl-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)), so the record's 2026-12 primary completion looks stale.

**Earlier resmetirom data in NASH (non-cirrhotic, histology endpoints)**
- MAESTRO-NASH (n=966 in primary population, 52 weeks) met both histology endpoints. Fibrosis improvement of at least one stage was 24.2% (80 mg) and 25.9% (100 mg) versus 14.2% placebo, p<0.001 ([NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2309000); [Birmingham repository](https://research.birmingham.ac.uk/en/publications/a-phase-3-randomized-controlled-trial-of-resmetirom-in-nash-with-/)). These were histology endpoints, not clinical outcomes.
- No clinical-outcome data exist from the trial itself. Investigators described outcomes as accruing over the 54-month plan ([NEJM](https://www.natap.org/2024/HIV/nejmoa2309000.pdf)).

**Cirrhosis-specific data (open-label only)**
- MAESTRO-NAFLD-1 compensated cirrhosis cohort: 122 patients, 113 completed two years ([PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12879063/)). Liver stiffness fell by about 6.7 kPa at two years ([Madrigal](https://ir.madrigalpharma.com/news-releases/news-release-details/madrigal-announces-new-two-year-data-compensated-mash-cirrhosis)). About 35% of confirmed F4 patients converted to F3 ([Medscape](https://www.medscape.com/viewarticle/resmetirom-reduces-liver-stiffness-mash-cirrhosis-2025a1000txt)). There was no placebo arm.
- Treatment interruption reversed gains, which were restored on resumption ([Madrigal](https://ir.madrigalpharma.com/news-releases/news-release-details/madrigal-presents-new-data-demonstrating-rezdiffrar-resmetirom)).

**Other drugs in this disease**
- Semaglutide in a 48-week cirrhosis trial improved weight and metabolic parameters but not fibrosis or hepatic outcomes ([ESSENCE review](https://www.oaepublish.com/articles/mtod.2026.13)).
- Efruxifermin's phase 2b SYMMETRY trial missed its week-36 primary endpoint in compensated cirrhosis (18% and 19% versus 13%); later effects were more evident by week 96 ([PMC review](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13358175/)).
- Survodutide's phase 3 LIVERAGE-Cirrhosis uses a composite outcome primary endpoint and is ongoing ([PMC review](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13358175/)).
- Obeticholic acid's REGENERATE, which had a clinical-outcome design, was stopped early after a regulatory setback. Its final results suggested a trend toward benefit on clinical outcomes ([HCPLive](https://www.hcplive.com/view/regenerate-final-results-for-obeticholic-acid-for-pre-cirrhotic-fibrosis-due-to-nash)).

**Base rate and comparator**
- I found no systematic base rate for composite clinical-outcome endpoints in NASH cirrhosis. Of nine network-meta-analysed cirrhosis RCTs, efruxifermin was the only agent significantly better than placebo for fibrosis improvement ([Gastro & Hepatol/NMA](https://www.gastroenterologyandhepatology.net/supplements/highlights-in-mash-from-the-aasld-2025-liver-meeting/)). That is a histology result, not a clinical-outcome result.
- An analyst on the Q3 call cited historical controlled F4 placebo event rates of roughly 2–3%. Management said the trial enriched for more advanced cirrhosis ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/healthcare/articles/madrigal-pharmaceuticals-inc-mdgl-q3-210542338.html)).

**Powering, interim analyses, and timing**
- The trial is event-driven and will not stop until enough events accrue, which could push the readout past 2027 ([TipRanks](https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/madrigal-earnings-call-highlights-rezdiffra-growth); [TokenPost](https://www.tokenpost.com/news/business/48432)).
- Management said event accrual is uneven, that blinded accrual details are not disclosed, and that dropout is within expectations ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/healthcare/articles/madrigal-pharmaceuticals-inc-mdgl-q3-210542338.html)).
- Between 25% and 30% of participants were on stable GLP-1 therapy at baseline, and GLP-1s are not permitted during the trial ([TipRanks](https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/madrigal-earnings-call-highlights-rezdiffra-growth)).
- The record's composite definition differs across mirrors. One lists all-cause mortality; another lists liver-related and cardiovascular mortality ([UCSD mirror](https://clinicaltrials.ucsd.edu/trial/NCT05500222)). Check the current protocol.
- I found no public interim efficacy analysis or design change.

**RESULT ALREADY PUBLIC:** not for NCT07037277. Atea says C-FORWARD topline results are expected in early 2027, later than the year-end 2026 guidance, so the record's 2026-12 primary completion date looks stale. [https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/11/09/3398942/0/en/atea-pharmaceuticals-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results-and-provides-business-update.html]

**Sister trial (C-BEYOND, NCT06868264, North America):** Same comparator, endpoint and design. It met non-inferiority in the mITT population: 93.91% SVR for BEM/RZR vs 94.75% for SOF/VEL at Week 24. [https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/atea-pharmaceuticals-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results-and-provides-business-update] This is company-reported; I found no peer-reviewed paper yet, and the company plans to present detailed data later. [https://ir.ateapharma.com/news-releases/news-release-details/atea-pharmaceuticals-meets-both-its-primary-and-secondary]

**Earlier trials of this regimen (Phase 2, NCT05904470):**
- Single-arm, open-label, n=275. SVR12 was 98% (208/213) in treatment-adherent patients, 95% regardless of adherence, and 88% in compensated cirrhosis. [https://ir.ateapharma.com/news-releases/news-release-details/atea-pharmaceuticals-announces-full-results-phase-2-study]
- No p-values or comparator; the endpoint was SVR12, not the trial's Week-24 endpoint.
- An investigator (Lawitz) noted Phase 2 was open-label and expected Phase 3 results to be similar. [https://www.contagionlive.com/view/hcv-therapy-demonstrates-98-sustained-virologic-response-at-12-weeks-post-treatment]

**Other diseases and other drugs in this mechanism:** I found nothing on bemnifosbuvir or ruzasvir outside HCV, and no Phase 3 data for other nucleotide-plus-NS5A combinations.

**Powering and design:**
- Trials are powered at 90% with a 5% non-inferiority margin, assuming about 95% in mITT. [https://finance.yahoo.com/news/atea-pharmaceuticals-q4-earnings-call-234744024.html?prefer_reader_view=1&prefer_safari=1]
- C-FORWARD's primary analysis is per-protocol (EMA preference), while C-BEYOND used mITT (FDA preference). [same source]
- Management said discontinuations occurred in C-BEYOND but that C-FORWARD remains adequately powered. [https://gloom.sh/stocks/avir/transcripts/q2-2026] This is a third-party transcript summary.

**Enrollment:** Completed June 2026, more than 880 patients, about 120 sites in 17 countries. [https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/06/25/3317395/0/en/Atea-Pharmaceuticals-Completes-Patient-Enrollment-in-Phase-3-C-FORWARD-Trial-Evaluating-Bemnifosbuvir-and-Ruzasvir-for-Treatment-of-Hepatitis-C-Virus.html] The CMO said cirrhotic enrollment "has not been an issue." [https://finance.yahoo.com/news/atea-pharmaceuticals-q4-earnings-call-234744024.html?prefer_reader_view=1&prefer_safari=1]

**Comparator and base rates:**
- SOF/VEL pooled SVR12 exceeded 94% across genotypes 1, 2 and 4, with lower rates likely in genotype 3. [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0168827816300083]
- In genotype 3 with compensated cirrhosis, SOF/VEL gave 91% (ASTRAL-3) and 96% (POLARIS-3) SVR12. [https://www.gastrojournal.org/article/S0016-5085(18)34684-5/fulltext]
- Implication: the comparator sits near 95%, so a 5-point margin is tight. Genotype mix in C-FORWARD (more non-1 genotypes) matters, and Atea's Phase 2 genotype-3 data were small.

**Schedule and timeline:** Atea said C-FORWARD topline results moved from year-end 2026 to early 2027. [https://ir.ateapharma.com/news-releases/news-release-details/atea-pharmaceuticals-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial]

**Evidence brief: NCT06989918 (MHB018A, active TED, Phase 3, China)**

**Result status:** No topline result for this trial was found. Sponsor guidance is for China Phase 3 topline in Q3 2026 ([PR Newswire, June 2026](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/minghui-pharmaceutical-presents-compelling-phase-iii-results-for-mhb018a-a-novel-subcutaneous-anti-igf-1r-antibody-for-thyroid-eye-disease-in-an-oral-presentation-at-endo-2026-the-endocrine-societys-annual-meeting-302799997.html)). That window has passed without a release I could find. The record's primary completion (2026-12) is later than that guidance.

**1. Earlier MHB018A data (Phase 1/2, ENDO 2026)**
- At 450 mg, the active-TED cohort (n=32) reached an 81% proptosis response at Week 12 ([sponsor PR, Dec 2025](https://www.biopharmaboardroom.com/news/53/4127/minghui-pharma-secures-fda-ind-clearance-to-launch-global-phase-3-trials-of-mhb018a-in-thyroid-eye-disease.html)). The same data showed 76% at Week 24 in chronic TED ([BioSpectrum](https://www.biospectrumasia.com/news/35/27818/minghui-reports-phase-i-ii-data-for-mhb018a-in-thyroid-eye-disease.html)).
- The Phase 1/2 included a randomized double-blind phase, but I found no placebo-arm proptosis figures, p-values, or confidence intervals ([touchOPHTHALMOLOGY](https://touchophthalmology.com/insight/mhb018a-shows-clinical-activity-in-active-and-chronic-thyroid-eye-disease/)).
- Commentators note the 81% is a Week 12 figure, not the Week 24 timepoint this trial uses ([TechTimes](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/318460/20260616/thyroid-eye-disease-treatment-mhb018a-subcutaneous-shot-hits-81-proptosis-response.htm)).

**2. Same drug, other diseases:** None found.

**3. Same mechanism in active TED (Week 24 unless noted; placebo in parentheses)**
- Teprotumumab IV, OPTIC: 83% ([TechTimes](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/318460/20260616/thyroid-eye-disease-treatment-mhb018a-subcutaneous-shot-hits-81-proptosis-response.htm)).
- Teprotumumab SC (Amgen): 77% ([TechTimes](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/318460/20260616/thyroid-eye-disease-treatment-mhb018a-subcutaneous-shot-hits-81-proptosis-response.htm)).
- IBI311 (RESTORE-1, n=82): 85.8% vs 3.8%, P<.001 ([Ophthalmology Advisor](https://www.ophthalmologyadvisor.com/news/ibi311-igf1r-inhibitor-thyroid-eye-disease-efficacy/)).
- Elegrobart (REVEAL-1, n=132): 54% (Q4W) and 63% (Q8W) vs 18% ([Minichart](https://www.minichart.com.sg/2026/03/30/viridian-therapeutics-announces-positive-phase-3-results-for-elegrobart-in-active-thyroid-eye-disease-eyes-2027-fda-submission/)).
- Veligrotug (THRIVE): Week 15 rate of 70%, placebo-adjusted 64%, P<0.0001 ([Viridian](https://investors.viridiantherapeutics.com/news/news-details/2024/Viridian-Therapeutics-Announces-Positive-Topline-Results-from-Veligrotug-VRDN-001-Phase-3-THRIVE-Clinical-Trial-in-Patients-with-Active-Thyroid-Eye-Disease/default.aspx)).
- Lonigutamab (Phase 1/2, SC): 50–67% ([TechTimes](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/318460/20260616/thyroid-eye-disease-treatment-mhb018a-subcutaneous-shot-hits-81-proptosis-response.htm)).

**4. Endpoint base rates**
- Across these trials, the proptosis responder endpoint was met by every placebo-controlled IGF-1R Phase 3 I found. Placebo response in active disease ranged from about 4% to 18%.
- Chronic TED placebo response was lower: 8% for veligrotug in THRIVE-2 ([Endocrinology Advisor](https://www.endocrinologyadvisor.com/news/veligrotug-beneficial-for-patients-with-chronic-thyroid-eye-disease/)).
- I found no reported failures of this endpoint for this drug class in active TED.

**5. Sponsor statements on powering, interims, enrollment, delays**
- The record lists no data monitoring committee.
- I found no statements on power, interim analyses, enrollment problems, or design changes for the China trial.
- The sponsor has described its global Phase 3 as still to enroll, with first patient targeted for Q4 2026 ([PR Newswire](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/minghui-pharmaceutical-presents-compelling-phase-iii-results-for-mhb018a-a-novel-subcutaneous-anti-igf-1r-antibody-for-thyroid-eye-disease-in-an-oral-presentation-at-endo-2026-the-endocrine-societys-annual-meeting-302799997.html)).

**Bottom line:** The comparator (placebo) is weak, and same-class Phase 3 trials have produced large responses. The drug's own evidence is a small, uncontrolled-looking Week 12 figure, with no reported placebo p-values for MHB018A.

**Evidence brief: masupirdine Phase 3 (NCT05397639), CMAI primary endpoint**

**Result status:** No topline result is public as of 2026-11-22. The company's current guidance is topline data in Q2 2027, and it calls that timing a possibility, not a firm date ([BSE filing](https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachHis/ae33ce45-3ecd-4592-bebb-35e679582c5d.pdf); [Multibagg](https://www.multibagg.ai/market-pulse/articles/suven-masupirdine-phase-3-timeline-announcement-cmw3jmqme006qjk2rk30ruyf3)).

**Record discrepancies:** The sponsor reports 424 patients randomized against a planned 375, with last-patient-last-visit expected by end of December 2026 ([BSE filing](https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachHis/ae33ce45-3ecd-4592-bebb-35e679582c5d.pdf)). The record's site count (44) conflicts with the sponsor's June description of about 80 sites ([ScanX](https://scanx.trade/stock-market-news/companies/suven-life-sciences-reports-positive-dsmb-review-for-masupirdine-study/42096524)).

**Earlier trial (Phase 2a, NCT02580305):**
- The prespecified primary outcome showed no drug-placebo difference ([PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9828442/)).
- The agitation signal is a post hoc subgroup on the NPI-12, not the CMAI. In patients with baseline agitation, the 50 mg arm (n=53 vs 57 placebo) reached p<0.001 at Week 13 and the 100 mg arm reached p=0.007 ([PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9828442/)).
- Effect sizes at Week 13 were Cohen's d 0.32–0.50 ([Neurology abstract](https://n.neurology.org/content/98/18_Supplement/2172)). The trial enrolled 564 patients over 26 weeks ([NeurologyLive](https://www.neurologylive.com/view/phase-3-trial-uncover-therapeutic-potential-5-ht6-antagonist-masupirdine-treat-alzheimer-agitation)).

**Other diseases:** I found no clinical data for masupirdine outside Alzheimer's. The only other evidence is rodent aggression models ([PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11712933/)).

**Mechanism:** Earlier 5-HT6 antagonists tested for Alzheimer's cognition, including intepirdine and idalopirdine, were all discontinued for lack of efficacy ([Alzforum](https://www.alzforum.org/therapeutics/masupirdine)). I found no other 5-HT6 agitation trials.

**Same-endpoint comparators (CMAI):**
- Brexpiprazole, the approved comparator: the pooled analysis of two fixed-dose trials showed a 4.5-point CMAI difference (d=0.30), with placebo improving about 18 points over 12 weeks ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41591746/)). One trial was significant at p=0.040 for the 2 mg arm, while the flexible-dose trial was not significant at p=0.15 ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31708380/)).
- AXS-05: ADVANCE-1 met its CMAI endpoint (p=0.010 vs placebo) ([Alzheimer's & Dementia](https://alz-journals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/alz70859_099716)). ADVANCE-2 missed it (p=0.38) ([SEC exhibit](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1579428/000095017024140949/axsm-ex99_2.htm)).
- Base rate: I did not find a count of CMAI-primary agitation trials that met their endpoint. From the examples above, the outcome is mixed.

**Sponsor statements on powering, interims, and timing:**
- A prespecified unblinded interim analysis assessed sample-size adequacy. The DSMB recommended no increase ([ScanX](https://scanx.trade/stock-market-news/companies/suven-life-sciences-reports-positive-dsmb-review-for-masupirdine-study/42096524)). The filing does not report an efficacy readout from that interim ([MultiBagg](https://www.multibagg.ai/market-pulse/articles/suven-masupirdine-phase-3-timeline-announcement-cmw3jmqme006qjk2rk30ruyf3)).
- Timing has slipped. A 2023 abstract expected readout in Q1/Q2 2025 ([Alzheimer's & Dementia](https://alz-journals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/alz.074068)).
- Enrollment exceeded plan, and the CEO reported no major safety concerns ([Medical Dialogues](https://medicaldialogues.in/news/industry/pharma/suven-life-sciences-to-present-phase-3-masupirdine-phase-1-tenaclidine-data-at-alzheimers-conference-183609)).

**Not found:** Primary-endpoint results from any CMAI trial of masupirdine, and any statement on how the 50 mg and 100 mg arms are expected to compare.

**Evidence brief: NCT04442022 (SR-GDP vs R-GDP, XPORT-DLBCL-030)**

No result for this trial has been announced. I found no Phase 2 ORR or Phase 3 PFS readout.

**Most important finding: the confirmatory trial appears to have been abandoned**
- The FDA granted accelerated approval in 2020 and agreed that XPORT-DLBCL-030 could serve as the confirmatory trial ([Karyopharm, 2020](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2020/06/22/2051422/0/en/Karyopharm-Announces-FDA-Approval-of-XPOVIO-selinexor-for-the-Treatment-of-Patients-with-Relapsed-or-Refractory-Diffuse-Large-B-cell-Lymphoma-DLBCL.html)).
- In March 2026 the FDA asked the company to withdraw the indication due to the Company's inability to complete the confirmatory trial ([8-K summary](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/KPTI/8-k-karyopharm-therapeutics-inc-reports-material-event-43813b50f4fe.html)). The withdrawal was submitted on April 6, 2026 ([ASCO](https://www.asco.org/news-initiatives/policy-news-analysis/fda-withdraws-accelerated-approval-xpovio-dlbcl)).
- The company said development costs will cease for DLBCL.
- The record still shows the trial as active and not recruiting, with primary completion 2026-12. Check for a termination or withdrawal notice before relying on that date.

**Earlier trials of selinexor in this disease**
- Phase 1 SELINDA: the recommended phase 2 dose was 40 or 60 mg once weekly with an ORR of 60-80% ([Blood abstract](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0006497121033930)). This was single-arm and small.
- SADAL (single-arm Phase 2b, n=134): ORR was 29%, including 18 (13%) complete responses ([CancerNetwork](https://www.cancernetwork.com/view/fda-approves-oral-selinexor-for-r-r-dlbcl)). ORR was the endpoint, and it was not compared with a control.
- Retrospective Fudan series (n=22, selinexor + R-GDP): ORR 52.4% at median follow-up of 25.5 months ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41523246/)). Its PFS analysis had no statistical test ([AJCR](https://e-century.us/files/ajcr/15/12/ajcr0168608.pdf)).
- No randomized selinexor + R-GDP data were found.

**Comparator**
- R-GDP in patients ineligible for transplant is cited at ORR of ~50%, a CR rate of ~25%, and a median PFS and OS of 3 and 9 months (same Blood abstract). These are historical figures, not contemporaneous controls.

**Other diseases (same drug, same sponsor)**
- SENTRY (myelofibrosis, Phase 3): met the SVR35 co-primary, but the second co-primary endpoint of change in absolute total symptom score after 24 weeks was not statistically significant ([Clinical Trials Arena](https://www.clinicaltrialsarena.com/news/karyopharms-phase-iii-myelofibrosis-trial-delivers-mixed-results/)).
- XPORT-EC-042 (endometrial, Phase 3, PFS primary): median PFS of 12.75 months versus 7.43 months for placebo, with a hazard ratio of 0.76 (95% CI: 0.51–1.12) and a one-sided p-value of 0.0791 ([8-K](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/KPTI/8-k-karyopharm-therapeutics-inc-reports-material-event-39eb9b475386.html)). This is a close miss on a PFS primary.
- Other XPO1 inhibitors in DLBCL: not found.

**Endpoint base rate**
- I did not find a tally of how often Phase 3 R/R DLBCL trials have met PFS. A review of six Phase 3 R/R DLBCL trials (n=1,577) reported a strong association between PFS and OS ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41429401/)).

**Sponsor statements on powering, interim analyses, and enrollment**
- Nothing found on powering, interim analyses, or the Phase 2 dose selection outcome.
- Sponsor finances: management still cites substantial doubt about continuing as a going concern, and expects current funding to last into late Q3 2026.
